Delap made his Forest debut as a substitute at Anfield last weekend, his first notable action a quick throw-in that led to the penalty scored by Morgan Gibbs-White to earn a second-half lead. Only after the 2-2 draw did Glasner discover that Delap’s father, Rory, who played for Southampton and Stoke among others, knew a thing or two about throws. “I said: your father will be proud of you,” says Forest’s head coach. So, has Liam got a mammoth throw in his armoury? “No, I don’t think so,” he replies. “I would never, anyway: I’m a striker, I need to be in the box.”

View image in fullscreen Liam Delap was much in demand after impressing with a 12-goal league season at Ipswich. Photograph: Ryan Pierse/Getty Images

Delap relishes the blood and thunder of battle. Glasner loves how Forest’s marquee signing stands up to centre-backs, making the point that defenders are hardly “hugging and kissing you all the time” in the heat of duels. But Delap, who spent a decade at Derby before joining City, says he has learned to harness his aggression on the field, after periods of getting into trouble when he was a youngster.

“You have to be careful, but not shy away from who you are,” he says. “I’m always going to fight for everything, always be aggressive, determined. It goes back to the point about my brother, being little kids in the garden, going at each other: that’s me. Sometimes you need to control it and sometimes you need to be careful, but I think I play at my best when I’m on that edge of being … being horrible.”

Sports.title: Chaotic Crystal Palace transfer window leaves Pierre Sage to run the gamut of emotions
Sports.content:
At least Pierre Sage did his research before joining Crystal Palace in June. Having stepped into Oliver Glasner’s shoes after the most successful era in the club’s history, it has not been the easiest transition for the engaging Frenchman following defeats against Everton and Manchester City to start the new campaign, and amid uncertainty surrounding the futures of some of the Conference League winners’ key players.

Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta ended up staying at Selhurst Park despite interest from Liverpool and Aston Villa respectively, while Palace brought in four new players after missing out to Sunderland for Malick Fofana in one of deadline day’s most dramatic storylines. But Sage is sanguine about experiencing a typically chaotic first transfer window in south London, and relieved to be able to concentrate on events on the pitch before Saturday’s trip to Fulham.

“I knew that and I had to deal and adapt to that,” Sage said when asked about Palace’s reputation for doing late deals, a trend that has led to them signing 10 players on the final day in the past three summer windows. “But at the end the most important thing is to have the player or the profile we choose and that’s the case. I think we are in line with what we need.”

Glasner, who has been joined at Nottingham Forest from Palace by Daniel Muñoz, made no secret of his dissatisfaction at having to wait until deadline day to bring in players after Palace signed four in his first summer at the club in 2024. It’s not Sage’s style to make a similar fuss, even if he is understood to have expressed frustration over their efforts to recruit a top-class replacement for Maxence Lacroix when the France defender was sold to Chelsea in July.

His favoured target was Ismaëlo Ganiou from Lens, the 21-year-old a key competent in the team that won the Coupe de France and finished second in Ligue 1 under Sage last season. However, Lens were reluctant to sell one of their prized assets and Ganiou signed a new deal at the start of August, forcing Palace to explore other targets.

A deal for Joel Ordóñez of Club Brugge broke down as the Ecuador defender is still recovering from a broken foot, while attempts to sign Augsburg’s Chrislain Matsima and Raphaël Le Guen of Brest also came to nothing. The arrival of Axel Disasi and the teenager Honest Ahanor on loan will help plug the gap, yet there remain major doubts over whether Lacroix’s leadership at the back has been fully replaced.

View image in fullscreen One that got away: Malick Fofana chose Sunderland over Palace on deadline day. Photograph: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images

Having failed to lure Mamadou Sangaré from Lens, with the Mali midfielder opting to join Brentford instead, Sage was the driving force in Palace’s attempt to bring in Fofana from another of his former clubs, Lyon. That ultimately proved futile despite a series of phone calls to the Belgium forward on deadline day. “I’m really proud and happy with what the club did for that,” Sage insisted. “We fight a lot and sometimes you cannot give more than this, but we give our best in this situation. At the end, the player chooses.” It remains to be seen whether the signing of the Chile forward Dario Osorio from the Danish club Midtjylland on an initial loan with an obligation to buy next summer for £26m makes up for the disappointment given he plays mainly on the right flank.

Palace are well stocked in attacking areas having also signed Dwight McNeil and Evann Guessand – who has been left out of the squad for the Europa League – and kept hold of Sarr. The return of Ben Chilwell and late addition of Quinten Timber to midfield will add depth and are believed to have gone some way to satisfying Sage, not to mention Palace’s rejection of bids from unnamed sides for Adam Wharton. Manchester City and Chelsea were believed to be among those who showed an interest. “The club was strong with the situation, and I think the player is completely in line with that,” he said.

But after breaking their transfer record twice in January, for Jørgen Strand Larsen and Brennan Johnson – who was swapped for McNeil, with Everton – Palace’s summer net spend of almost £40m in profit was the second lowest in the division behind Aston Villa. Over the past five seasons, Hull and Coventry have both invested more than Palace’s £90m despite being in the Championship.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Sage was quick to reject suggestions he is unhappy with Palace’s summer signings and instead drew on his experiences from watching his parents run their brasserie in Belley, a town in the Ain region of eastern France. “I’m not frustrated – we are not a bank,” he said. “We do with what we have. My parents had a restaurant and I prefer every day there’s a lot of clients but it was not the case sometimes and we have to deal with that every day. In football it’s the same.”

View image in fullscreen Pierre Sage said of Palace’s transfer window: ‘I’m not frustrated, we’re not a bank.’ Photograph: Malcolm Fell/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock

The absences of Sarr and Mateta, the latter of which had his hopes of leaving scuppered by a hamstring injury that will keep him out for another three weeks, will not help Palace’s chances against Fulham. Sage expects Sarr back from a groin injury for the game against Ipswich next Saturday but said the Senegal forward “needs time” after being affected by Liverpool’s interest, which led to his agent releasing a statement criticising the player’s treatment.

It will not have escaped Sage’s attention that Glasner won three times at Craven Cottage in 2025, including a quarter-final victory on the way to winning the FA Cup. After the week he has had, more of the same would do against another team who have yet to get off the mark in the league this season.

Sports.title: WSL transfer talking points: three things we learned from the data
Sports.content:
The Women’s Super League’s summer transfer window has closed before the start of the 2026-27 season. The finances involved are microscopic compared with the £3.4bn that Premier League clubs spent on new players but the data provides three key points of interest: which club has made the biggest improvement to their squad, who is banking on stability, and how the women’s game has outsmarted its male equivalent.

Arsenal have the most improved squad

Many transfers in women’s football occur without the fee being disclosed, which deprives us of the conventional shorthand for assessing player quality. Thankfully there is Soccerdonna, the arm of Transfermarkt that covers women’s football. It carries estimated market values of players in euros. Using these, we can see by how much clubs have improved their squads.

Arsenal’s new additions have a combined value of €3.9m, slightly more than the €3.5m of talent that London City Lionesses have gained this summer. The entire squads of eight of the 14 teams in the 2026-27 WSL are worth less than these figures, which highlights the impact the new players should have. Indeed, London City’s new two-time Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas is valued at €1.15m, which is more than the entire Charlton squad and not far behind the roster at Crystal Palace.

West Ham could argue they have added the most to their squad as the combined market value of their new players (€1.02m) is more than the corresponding amount for the players who remain from last season (€0.96m). Having finished 10th after winning only three of their opening 19 matches, improvements were clearly required.

Clubs have kept more settled squads

While supporters are most excited by new signings, departees are just as relevant to the health of a squad. Or at least they are if they made significant contributions in the previous season.

West Ham had to make additions as they lost players that contributed 6,322 minutes in the 2025-26 WSL, 29% of their total. Chief among those leaving was the goalkeeper Kinga Szemik, who started 19 of 22 games. Only Martina Fernández (1,950 minutes for Everton) and Keira Flannery (1,891 at Charlton) left current WSL clubs and played more minutes last season.

Teams may have learned from 12 months ago. Brighton lost 9,584 minutes of playing time from their 2024-25 squad in the summer 2025 window and went on to finish two places lower last season. Liverpool also said goodbye to a higher share of their playing time than anyone has in this transfer window (6,406 minutes), and started the campaign very slowly.

Output could be a greater issue than time played. Manchester City and Aston Villa have both lost players who contributed at least 13 combined goals and assists last season in Kerolin and Kirsty Hanson respectively. The difference between these clubs is that the champions can absorb the cost of that exit far more easily. The 17 goal contributions Villa have lost from last season through players leaving constitute 36.2% of their total, the highest proportion of the teams who were in the WSL in 2025-26.

The WSL is far better prepared for transfer windows than the Premier League

The Premier League endured a ridiculous deadline day on Tuesday. Around a sixth of players signed by clubs in the latest transfer window completed their deals on 1 September. Just over a third of the money that went on transfer fees this summer was spent after the 2026-27 season had already begun.

Things have been rather more organised in the WSL. Granted, its window closed before the new campaign gets under way and they didn’t have a World Cup clogging up the summer this year. But where the Premier League had completed only 83% of eventual total signings when deadline day began, the WSL made that proportion four weeks ago.

The obvious explanation would be that lower-finance deals are easier to complete. Yet Fifa recently revealed global spending on transfer fees in women’s football had increased by 83.6% year-on-year. Spending on agents fees by WSL clubs grew by 75% in the year up to 3 February 2026 too. The transfer business remains efficient even while the sums involved are rapidly increasing.

Men’s football will always have much more money but it could benefit from the transfer expertise and planning in the women’s game.

Sports.title: Manchester City failed to land Spain pair in scramble for Miedema cover
Sports.content:
Atlético Madrid rejected a bid of more than £500,000 from Manchester City for the Spain midfielder Fiamma Benítez on the Women’s Super League’s transfer deadline day, the Guardian can reveal.

The WSL champions are understood to have tried hard to add attacking-midfielder reinforcements before the English summer window closed on Thursday at 11pm BST, largely in light of news that their No 10 Vivianne Miedema could be out for at least the rest of 2026 with a knee injury.

However, Atlético are understood to view Benítez as a key player and a future national team star and were not prepared to let the 22-year-old go. In 2022 Benítez helped Spain win the Under-19 Euros and Under-20 Women’s World Cup and she helped her country win the 2024 Women’s Nations League.

City then made an even later move for Everton’s Spain international Ornella Vignola, who can play in midfield or on the wing. A bid of about £400,000 is understood to have been turned down by Everton, largely because they felt they would not have time to source a suitable replacement but also because of Vignola’s importance to Scott Phelan’s side.

It was also widely reported that City attempted to bring in the Nigeria midfielder Jennifer Echegini from Paris Saint-Germain, but multiple sources have told the Guardian that PSG made clear they were not willing to sell the 25-year-old. PSG had agreed to sell the France defender Élisa De Almeida to Arsenal for a fee believed to be just over £500,000, and they were not prepared to lose two key players in one day.

City completed one deadline-day deal, bringing in England’s Anna Moorhouse on loan from Orlando Pride until the end of January, adding good-quality depth to their goalkeeping ranks after Khiara Keating moved to Liverpool on a free in July.

Although City were left scrambling unsuccessfully for a midfielder on Thursday, it was a positive summer for the club, not least because they began the summer with their most important deal, retaining the services of the WSL’s Golden Boot winner Khadija Shaw with a lucrative new contract. Andrée Jeglertz’s side begin their title defence at home to promoted Birmingham City on Sunday.

Meanwhile, Arsenal will face both of last season’s Women’s Champions League finalists during this season’s League Phase after receiving the trickiest-looking draw of the three English sides involved.

Renée Slegers’ side, who won the Champions League in 2025, will travel to holders Barcelona and host runners-up OL Lyonnes as their two pot-one opponents. Chelsea travel to OL Lyonnes, Sonia Bompastor’s former side, and also host Paris Saint-Germain and Roma. City, who were in pot three, were handed home matches against PSG and Real Madrid, as well as a trip to Bayern Munich.

Arsenal’s other ties include a visit to Milan to face Inter, who pulled off the surprise of the qualifying rounds by eliminating the two-time champions Wolfsburg on penalties. City will also be away to Inter, who finished second in Serie A last season.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

There is a lot of similarity between Chelsea and Manchester City’s opponents; they both face PSG and Austria Wien at home and travel to Swedish side BK Hacken, who won last season’s inaugural Women’s Europa Cup.

The 18-team League phase gets under way on 22-23 September and the full fixture list is expected to be published within the next 24 hours. Each side plays six other teams overall – two from each of pot one, pot two and pot three. Teams from the same nation could not face each other.

The top four teams after the six matchdays in the League phase will qualify automatically for the quarter-finals, which begin in March. The teams finishing between fifth and 12th will contest the knockout phase playoffs in February, to fight for the four remaining quarter-final places. This season’s final will be held in Warsaw, Poland, in May.

The three English side’s full lists of opponents:

Manchester City PSG (h), Bayern Munich (a), Real Madrid (h), BK Hacken (a), Austria Wien (h), Inter (a).

Arsenal OL Lyonnes (h), Barcelona (a), Benfica (h), Paris FC (a), HB Koge (h), Inter (a).

Chelsea PSG (h), OL Lyonnes (a), Roma (h), BK Hacken (a), Austria Wien (h), OH Leuven (a).

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
Sports.content:
1 Can Wirtz find his best for Liverpool?

Florian Wirtz is easing himself into his second season at Liverpool after a forgettable first. There were signs of promise against Nottingham Forest, where he set up the second equaliser and would have had a goal of his own if not for an offside in the buildup. It is clear the German needs to become more influential as a No 10 given the quality of players he has around him, especially after the expensive arrival of Bradley Barcola this week. Bruno Fernandes showed there is plenty of fun for an attacking midfielder to have against Ipswich and Wirtz can follow suit as a protagonist. Liverpool have drawn both their opening fixtures 2-2 and need something to kickstart their campaign, with a Friday night visit to promoted opposition a fine place to do so. Wirtz should cause problems but, if he does not, the internal competition will be after his spot. Will Unwin

Ipswich v Liverpool (Friday 8pm, all times BST)

2 Red Bull gives you wings

Verticality, intensity and hard pressing are likely to be the order of the day at St James’ Park, where two German graduates of the Red Bull stable meet on Saturday at lunchtime. Newcastle’s new manager, Matthias Jaissle, is a former head coach of Red Bull Salzburg, while Bournemouth’s Marco Rose has managed Salzburg and RB Leipzig. “We have the same idea of how we want to play football,” said Jaissle – and Rose knows what to expect from Eddie Howe’s successor. “Matthias and me were several years in the style of Red Bull,” he said. “Everyone knows how we work. You can see it clearly. He’s a good coach. He’s brought his ideas really quickly into the Newcastle team. They are playing quite intense, they have clear pressing patterns that are different from before.” Louise Taylor

Newcastle v Bournemouth (Saturday 12.30pm)

View image in fullscreen Matthias Jaissle is looking for back-to-back league wins with Newcastle. Photograph: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

3 Bees plot left-wing raid on Black Cats

Saturday’s meeting between two of the Premier League’s best-run clubs, Brentford and Sunderland, promises to one of the best contests of the weekend, with both sides physical, technical and superbly coached. Brentford, in particular, have made a terrific start to the season, the left side of their team looking especially dangerous. Keane Lewis-Potter provides impetus from full-back, with Mamadou Sangaré backing up strong ball-winning and carrying with intelligent passing, while Kevin Schade offers a threat in behind and, increasingly, in front of goal. All of which suggests a difficult afternoon for Thomas Meunier, Sunderland’s likely right-back who, at 34, has plenty of experience but might struggle with the athletic questions asked of him. He will, though, be able to rely on assistance from Noah Sadiki, whose nous, work ethic and running power will be invaluable in defending Sunderland’s right flank. How that battle plays out will go a long way towards deciding the game. Daniel Harris

Brentford v Sunderland (Saturday 3pm)

4 Chema looks another astute Brighton buy

We can be sure any player Brighton buy has delivered the data metrics employed by the owner, Tony Bloom. But Chema Andrés, the 21-year-old midfielder just signed from Stuttgart, also nails the eye test. He was signed for £18.9m and it’s already tempting to speculate how sizeable the mark-up will be when Brighton sell him on. If we remember we’re talking about a sport, it’s impossible not to be excited about what the former Real Madrid academy midfielder brings to Fabian Hürzeler’s team. A No 6 of the old school, Chema offers economical movement but extravagant intelligence, evident in his passing and anticipation. Even if this weekend’s game against Leeds comes too early for him to be handed a start, he will make an impact soon enough. DH

Brighton v Leeds (Saturday 3pm)

5 An early basement battle at the Cottage

It’s been a tricky summer for Crystal Palace despite their Conference League win. Oliver Glasner has gone, with two key defenders in Daniel Muñoz and Maxence Lacroix also departing and Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaïla Sarr trying their best to do likewise. This upheaval has left Pierre Sage, whose existing relationship with Malick Fofana wasn’t enough to secure the Lyon winger’s signature, with major problems. The former Lens coach is seeking to replace the club’s most successful manager while learning what works in a new league, with new players and without three mainstays. It wasn’t especially surprising to see Palace lose their first two matches, while Fulham have also been beaten twice while seeking to bed in a new coach and arrivals. More troubling for both teams is that the promoted sides look competitive. Hull and Ipswich have performed well and won games, while Coventry are better than they’ve shown so far. Though it’s far too early to talk about relegation, this already feels like a game of significance for two sides struggling for momentum. DH

Fulham v Crystal Palace (Saturday 3pm)

6 O’Reilly to step into Rodri role for City?

Manchester City spent more than £300m on new midfielders in this transfer window, but look light in the No 6 role, with Rodri and Nico González both departing. Ayyoub Bouaddi, bought as Rodri’s long-term successor, is only 18, so Enzo Maresca’s plan is to ease him into first-team action. The Manchester City manager deployed Marc Guéhi in a holding midfield role against Bournemouth, and is also confident Nico O’Reilly can switch from left-back to operate there. O’Reilly may line up at the base of midfield for Coventry’s visit, with City seeking a third straight win. Maresca is also not fazed by Omar Marmoush’s departure on an initial loan to Spurs, with Iliman Ndiaye arriving on deadline day and Antoine Semenyo also an able deputy centre-forward if Erling Haaland is unavailable. Jamie Jackson

Manchester City v Coventry (Saturday 3pm)

7 Delap to be thrown in against shaky Spurs

Liam Delap came off the bench against Liverpool and helped create Nottingham Forest’s second goal with quick thinking from a throw-in. The striker cost £45m from Chelsea but missed out on an intense pre-season after Xabi Alonso decided he was surplus to requirements, so needs to build fitness. Considering Tottenham’s major flaws thus far, it would make sense for Delap to be given the chance to spearhead the Forest attack. The former England Under-21s striker is the ideal No 9, quick, strong and a capable finisher, but needs to get all these attributes sharpened up. An outing against fragile opposition could speed up the process. Tottenham are bottom of the league having conceded five and scored none in two games, and compared with Chris Wood or Igor Jesus, Delap is a far scarier foe, as Oliver Glasner will know. WU

Nottingham Forest v Tottenham (Saturday 3pm)

8 Six points, seven signings for happy Hull

They may have nabbed two wins in as many games upon their return to the Premier League but Hull were still not happy with their squad, seven new players arriving in the final week of the window. That means the Tigers have made 19 signings since promotion, which is an impressive turnover in personnel. Sergej Jakirovic needs to decide whether to incorporate these potential upgrades into his starting XI as soon as possible or make them earn the shirts from those who have accumulated six points. No one has let down the head coach or the fans over 180 minutes, so it would be harsh to drop anyone but, equally, having spent so much money on acquisitions, it could be argued that the sooner they get on the pitch, the quicker they will gel. It is not an easy decision for Jakirovic to make but he values loyalty and will want to challenge the mentality of the new arrivals – no one will walk into the side he has built. WU

Hull v Aston Villa (Saturday 5.30pm)

View image in fullscreen Elliot Stroud, one of Hull’s 19 summer signings, in action during their 1-0 win at Coventry. Photograph: Neal Simpson/Getty Images/Allstar

9 Everton fans react to dismal deadline day

There are parallels between Manchester United’s visit to Hill Dickinson Stadium and their 3-0 win at Goodison Park in 2023 in the sense they will face a furious Everton crowd, and for the second time in four seasons the anger will not be directed towards them. Three years ago it was the Premier League in Evertonians’ sights after the record 10-point deduction that had just been imposed on the club. This time it is Everton’s owners, The Friedkin Group, in the firing line after the club’s shambolic end to the transfer window. There will be no flag displays inside the stadium after the group responsible for organising them, the 1878s, withdrew their support and there are calls for a “not a pound in the ground” campaign in response to the owners making a profit on transfers while leaving David Moyes with a weaker squad. Everton have started the season positively on the pitch, but are now surrounded by problems of their owners’ making. Andy Hunter

Everton v Manchester United (Sunday 2pm)

10 Chelsea face litmus test in London derby

You have to go back to the start of the 2021-22 season, when Arsenal had Rob Holding and Pablo Marí in central defence, for the last time Chelsea beat their north London rivals, a run of 11 matches in all competitions. But they came close to ending that sequence in the 1-1 draw at Stamford Bridge last season before things began to unravel for Enzo Maresca, and the Italian’s successor, Xabi Alonso, will head to the Emirates to face his old friend Mikel Arteta in a competitive match for the first time as a manager full of confidence after winning his opening two games. Chelsea’s new-look front three of Cole Palmer, João Pedro and Morgan Rogers can certainly cause Arsenal problems, although the question is whether a defence that has conceded five goals can keep out the champions. Ed Aarons

Arsenal v Chelsea (Sunday 4.30pm)

Sports.title: Tough start for PSG but Luis Enrique has faith in burst of ‘new energy’ from signings
Sports.content:
“It’s like we’re at school,” Luis Enrique quipped as he entered the press conference room, hearing the journalists respond in unison to his hearty bonjour.

His remark was fitting on the eve of Paris Saint-Germain’s first home match of the season, which lines up nicely with France’s rentrée, the term for the nationwide return to school and the office at the start of September. Although the new campaign is in full swing by now, the team have had to wait several weeks before making their return to the Parc des Princes, where they welcome second place Monaco on Friday night.

The league champions were due to start the season by hosting Rennes on the first day, but successive heatwaves over the summer had damaged the Parc des Princes pitch to the extent that the match was instead moved to Brittany. Rennes were also hoping to host the return match in March as scheduled, but the league authorities instead switched the two fixtures around in the calendar.

This year’s rentrée has not exactly seen a swift return to business as usual for the perennial Ligue 1 champions. Since beating Aston Villa to retain the Uefa Super Cup last month, PSG have lost the Trophée des Champions to Lens and drawn their first two league matches.

Late comebacks in the latter two fixtures have helped paper over the cracks of unconvincing displays against the league’s middle powers. A late double from Ferran Torres on debut rescued a point against Rennes, while a Vitinha-led revival saw PSG claw back a similar deficit in stoppage time in Lille.

“We’ve had less of a pre-season, so it’s been difficult,” summer signing Lucas Digne explained on Thursday after an open training session. “It’s not an excuse, but it’s an assessment.”

Admittedly, PSG’s first four domestic opponents of the season will have all been teams involved in Europe. “It hasn’t been the easiest combination of matches,” the head coach, Luis Enrique, said in his press conference later in the day. “But we’ve had to accept it and prepare for them.”

View image in fullscreen Ferran Torres scored twice on his PSG debut to rescue a point against Rennes. Photograph: Franco Arland/Getty Images

PSG now habitually click into gear mid-season, once the Champions League knockouts begin to appear on the horizon. A defeat to Monaco on Friday, though, could spark a minor crisis and precipitate the need for the team to be back at their full powers.

In any case, Luis Enrique was cryptic when asked about when his team would be at their best: “It depends on a lot of factors which are out of my control,” he said. “My job is just to find the best 11 players for each match.” The fact that his reigning champions are winless in three has ostensibly done little to dampen the 56-year-old’s optimism for his fourth season in charge.

“Do you think that losing tomorrow means we’re out of the title race?” Luis Enrique asked reporters on Thursday afternoon. “Our aim will be to beat a team that we lost to at home last season. It won’t be easy, especially considering they have a manager in Filipe Luís who takes a brave approach.”

View image in fullscreen The Paris Saint-Germain head coach, Luis Enrique, is hoping his team will be back to their best when they host Monaco. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

The Spaniard was also keen to stress the minor squad overhaul which took place over the summer. “We haven’t sold any of the players who started the Champions League final and we’ve bought some young players. We’ll have to wait and see what they can bring.”

While the starting XI that retained the Champions League title remains intact, Les Parisiens have replaced most of the supporting cast. All of Gonçalo Ramos, Lee Kang-in, Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have moved on, amounting to over €300m (£258m) in sales. Torres, Maghnes Akliouche and Mika Godts make up the reigning champions’ new frontline depth options, with Digne being the other senior arrival.

“Those players were important in our quest for trophies, but we needed new energy in the team,” Luis Enrique said.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

For the head coach, the toughest departure to make up for will be Bradley Barcola’s. The French international’s move, Luis Enrique explained, was a “special case”, given that he “grew a lot and helped the team grow” during his three years in the capital.

View image in fullscreen Mika Godts joined PSG from Ajax this summer. Photograph: Joachim Azouze/PSG/Getty Images

“He wanted to have a greater role in the team, and that’s not something I’m able to guarantee to any player,” the Spaniard said. “He was an important player and a great person, his teammates loved him. It was his decision and we have to accept it, I wish him all the best.”

The prospect of playing under Luis Enrique was seemingly the primary attraction for the summer arrivals, all of whom spoke to the press during Thursday’s open day at the club’s training ground.

“He was like a footballing father to me when I played for him in the national team,” Torres said of his compatriot. “He believed in me and wanted to bring me here, so I want to repay that confidence,” the former Barcelona man added, before stressing that he would be content to play wherever the head coach needed him. “He gives the front three a lot of freedom to move around, which makes things difficult for our opponents.”

“He’s a great coach, so I was happy to hear that he wanted me here,” Godts said. “He likes players who are versatile, and I’m ready to play anywhere, that’s not an issue,” the Belgian winger continued, “I’ll play on the left, on the right, as a No 10, even as a No 9.”

Monaco, although rocked by a chaotic end to the transfer window, are shaping up to be the sternest of PSG’s early-season tests. They are the only team in the league yet to drop points, and saw off Marseille last week with a double from the early-season breakout star Paris Brunner.

As they prepare to take to the brand new Parc des Princes pitch, it would be difficult to imagine a more enticing opponent to mark the rentrée at home for Luis Enrique’s new and old students.

Sports.title: David Moyes reveals he hasn't spoken to Everton's new owners since disastrous deadline day
Sports.content:
David Moyes reveals he hasn't spoken to Everton's new owners since disastrous deadline day

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

David Moyes has claimed Everton's new owners are 'still finding' their way at the club, and revealed he has not spoken to them since Tuesday's frantic transfer deadline day.

The Toffees bid farewell to Iliman Ndiaye and Beto late in the window, leaving Moyes with just one natural centre forward in Thierno Barry. Tim Iroegbunam and Nathan Patterson also left, and any positivity from the arrivals of Jack Grealish and Ainsley Maitland-Niles was soured with the collapsed deal for Folarin Balogun.

Moyes now has just 18 senior outfield players, resulting in fury among the fanbase, directed towards the club's owners, The Friedkin Group. The Everton Fans' Forum has since issued a lengthy statement criticising the club, while influential fan group The 1878s is standing down its in-ground flag displays.

Reports this week have suggested the Friedkin Group, which also owns Italian side Roma, could be looking for outside investment.

Asked about that matter, Moyes replied: 'I've had no conversations with them, and certainly not on any investment. That's beyond my jurisdiction.

'I think if you want to have success, you need to be aligned on the same things. All those parts are so important. I think we have new owners who are finding their way in at the club. I think as we get to know each other a bit better, it will get better.'

David Moyes has admitted he is yet to speak to Everton's owners on the back of their deadline day nightmare

Moyes also added Everton needed to sell late in the market, hence the decision to allow Ndiaye to join City.

The former Manchester United manager also said there was no truth to reports claiming Chelsea made a late approach for midfielder James Garner, while he admitted Everton may look to the free-agent market to help cover any deficiencies in the squad.

'(I'm) disappointed we didn't do more business. Disappointed things didn't go our way in the end.'

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher says Liverpool should have let 'cult hero' leave as one of two who are 'never going to play' after omissions from 25-man squad
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher has suggested Liverpool should have let 'cult hero' Wataru Endo leave the club because he is 'never going to play' under Andoni Iraola.

Iraola has a handful of new players at his disposal this season following the arrivals of the likes of Jeremy Jacquet, Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola, while stars such as Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate have all departed.

This week, the Spaniard has had to select a 25-man squad for the league phase of the Champions League, meaning some unlucky names would be omitted.

Among them were Endo, who is yet to play under Iraola, and Federico Chiesa, who has had a hard time of things since joining the Reds in 2024.

Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike and Conor Bradley, meanwhile, are all battling long-term injuries, yet were still included.

And former Liverpool defender Carragher has called for justice. Speaking on The Overlap, he said: 'Liverpool have got two players in the squad who are never going to play. And there are all these quotas, you can only have 17 (non-homegrown) players and all that.

Jamie Carragher (pictured) has suggested Liverpool should have sold 'cult hero' Wataru Endo

Endo (right) has been left out of Liverpool's Champions League squad and found game time hard to come by

'They have got Chiesa and Endo. It's like they are never going to kick a ball.'

He added: 'Endo should have been moved on. He has done great, a bit of a cult hero.'

The Japan international played 12 times last season as he battled injuries and selection, with game time in the Premier League especially hard to come by.

He joined the club in the summer of 2023 under Jurgen Klopp, but has never really settled in the team.

Chiesa, meanwhile, struggled for minutes under Arne Slot and it appears it will be the same story under Iraola. He made just five starts last season, while he has missed the opening of this campaign through injury. Endo was an unused substitute in the draws with Newcastle and Nottingham Forest.

The duo may now have to wait for cup games to feature for the Reds, though can still feature in the league too.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick insists he's 'largely happy' with Manchester United's transfer business after quiet deadline day... and reveals surprise name as Luke Shaw's left back deputy
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick insists he's 'largely happy' with Manchester United's transfer business after quiet deadline day... and reveals surprise name as Luke Shaw's left back deputy

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Michael Carrick insists he is 'largely' happy with the transfer window despite Manchester United's failure to sign a new left back or striker.

United's £163million spend on midfielders Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and teenage winger Tynan Thompson was significantly less than their biggest Premier League rivals and even some of the newly-promoted clubs.

It has raised concerns that United are short of cover for left back Luke Shaw and have not strengthened in attack after turning down an offer for Joshua Zirkzee late in the transfer window from Everton – their opponents on Merseyside on Sunday.

Carrick maintained that he is happy with his squad while acknowledging that United could have done more and must rely on some players filling the gaps by being flexible.

'What squad is ever the perfect squad?' he said. 'You've always got to find ways of adapting. When you're building and going through a period where we're trying to get to the top, you've got to make steps. It's not going to be one hit. It's not just an instant fix and you finish top of the league and you stay there.

'You can always look at it, and there's other things you possibly could have done. Some things become available, some don't. That's just part of evolving the group.

Michael Carrick has insisted he is happy with Manchester United's transfer window despite the club failing to strengthen in a number of areas

'The situation is what it is, in terms of finances and what we can work with. I think for what we've spent, we've certainly made the most of it, without a shadow of a doubt – if not even more than that because of the players we've brought in.

'Largely, I think we're in a good place. So we've got players that are flexible as well throughout the whole team and can play in different positions. As you go through a season, you always need that. So, largely pretty happy, yeah.

'We went into the window wanting to come out stronger from the group that we had last season, and we've definitely added to that. I think we've done a lot of good work in that respect.

'Certainly, the players that we've brought into the group, I'm absolutely delighted with. I think we've done some really good business there for the quality and the level of player that we've got. I'm really, really happy with that.'

Having focussed on a midfield rebuild this summer, United will strengthen in defence at the end of the season after shelving a bid for Newcastle left back Lewis Hall and deciding against a number of options including a deadline-day move for Manchester City's Rayan Ait-Nouri.

Carrick backed Patrick Dorgu to be an option at left back after employing him further up the field throughout his tenure.

'He can certainly play there,' Carrick said. 'He has done, without doubt. I'm not sitting here saying he can't do that. It's just the way we've been since I've been here.

'He actually has been injured, unfortunately, for some time. So, for me, he's almost like a new player to have, and it's almost like a new signing in some ways because he's added so much to the group.

'He's played off the right for Denmark, scored a great goal in the summer playing off the right in a forward position. He can play left-back.'

Zirkzee was expected to leave but ended up staying despite interest from Fiorentina and Juventus, and a late loan bid from Everton. Instead of lining up against United at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, the Dutchman is set to be in Carrick's squad.

'For sure, Josh is important,' added the United boss. 'Josh is happy here and I have a really good relationship with him. What he wants is to play more than he has done and that's good, the healthy competition for places.

'Josh can do some really top things, I've seen it myself. I'm looking forward to him doing that a little bit more often for us.'

Sports.title: Entitled influencers moan they were kicked out of US Open and stripped of free passes after breaking crucial rule
Sports.content:
Entitled influencers moan they were kicked out of US Open and stripped of free passes after breaking crucial rule

The US Open's influencer controversy has reached boiling point. Amid the scrutiny surrounding the content creators invading Flushing Meadows, two have revealed that they were given the boot.

The Grand Slam has attracted new fans to the sport in recent years but this year's tournament has seemingly become increasingly overrun with influencers.

But the tournament found itself down a pair of the glamorous online socialites on Thursday when two were shown the door.

Meg Radice and Audrey Jongens, two NYC-based influencers who run the social media account The VIP List, claimed their credentials were revoked just hours after they committed a US Open cardinal sin.

The pair posted photos of their credentials on social media when they went to have dinner at a restaurant they had partnered with for the tournament.

'We post our credentials on our story. We go to our favorite restaurant. Have a nice steak dinner. We're downing Honey Deuces. We're having a great time, haven't even made it to court yet,' Redice told TMZ.

Two influencers have claimed that their US Open credentials were revoked this week

Meg Radice and Audrey Jongens said they were booted after posting their credentials online

'Within two hours of us leaving, we were told we could no longer use our credentials. We were heartbroken and we still are,' Jongens added.

Redice and Jongens received the passes through through a partnership with one of their favorite restaurants at the Open, then posted photos of the credentials to Instagram Stories this week.

They insisted that they were unaware they had broken any rules by sharing their credentials and have attended the tournament for the past three years.

The duo described themselves as 'diehard' tennis fans and said that they had intended to film content at the Grand Slam over the course of the two weeks, branding it a 'dream' opportunity.

'We were there to be respectful and follow the rules and just have a good time and show content to our followers about how amazing the US Open is,' Jongens added to TMZ.

'We were like, what do you mean? We had our credentials just stripped away within two hours before we even get to see a match. How does this happen?' Radice questioned.

'It was taken away like that. Just because we wanted to show how hot we looked in our credentials,' Radice added.

The pair pleaded with the USTA to allow them to return, saying: 'We don't even need an apology, we just want to go back.'

Radice and Jongens are NYC-based influencers who run the social media account The VIP Lis

They received the passes through through a partnership with one of their favorite restaurants

The duo described themselves as 'diehard' tennis fans, intending to film content at the event

They bemoaned the fact that they had cancelled plans for the two weeks and planned their outfits to be able to attend the event.

This year's tournament has seen the number of influencers at the event almost boule with the USTA credentialing 100 content creators.

Yet, the impromptu photoshoot between points, chatting and moving around have caused quite the stir at Arthur Ashe, leaving traditional tennis fans disgruntled over the lack of etiquette.

Earlier in the week, Naomi Osaka was forced to wait until the chair umpire had chided a group of spectators in one of Arthur Ashe's hospitality suites.

'Guys, please, in the suite behind me, please thank you guys, please take your seat,' the chair umpire announced to the stadium, as the broadcast camera panned to a group milling freely within their prime seats, taking pictures and talking.

Elsewhere in the stands, another spectator was heard calling out: 'The players are ready!'

When the stadium had stilled somewhat, Osaka returned to her serve but struggled with her ball toss, apologizing as she reset.

Guests of a US Open hospitality suite were told off by a chair umpire for taking pictures during a game, seemingly using a portable light (ringed)

One social media user called out 'influencers' for taking pictures while action was ongoing

Footage captured from another spectator of the group on social media later showed them posing as a group, allegedly during a game, with a person who appeared to be a member of US Open staff holding up a portable light to help them capture the shot.

The social media clip showed another spectator on the same evening posing in front of the court with a portable light, also allegedly during live matchplay.

When contacted by Daily Mail Sport for comment on the incident, Brendan McIntyre, head of US Open communications said: 'We want our fans and guests to have an incredible time when they attend the US Open, but we also need to ensure that does not interfere with the action and competition on the court.

'These instances happen infrequently, and similar to when crowd noise reaches a certain level, our chair umpires have the ability to address the crowd when they occur.'

Sports.title: Unai Emery explains why he left Roy Keane's £30m son-in-law Taylor Harwood-Bellis OUT of Aston Villa's Champions League squad - just two days after defender said 'I can't wait to show what I can do' in the competition
Sports.content:
Unai Emery explains why he left Roy Keane's £30m son-in-law Taylor Harwood-Bellis OUT of Aston Villa's Champions League squad - just two days after defender said 'I can't wait to show what I can do' in the competition

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Unai Emeryy has left £30million signing Taylor Harwood-Bellis out of Aston Villa’s squad for the Champions League phase.

The defender was signed from Southampton towards the end of August but has not been included in the 25-man squad, even though there are only three other orthodox centre-backs on the list.

Villa say the decision is not related to the UEFA settlement agreement, which means they can spend no more than they earn on transfers and wages.

‘It’s a hard decision,’ said Villa boss Emery, who also left 17-year-old forward Brian Madjo out in favour of Tammy Abraham – even though Villa wanted to sell Abraham this summer. Madjo is currently injured and will miss at least one European fixture.

‘Taylor was the last player to arrive in the window and we can get balance with Lamare Bogarde playing at centre-back, and even Boubacar Kamara can play there.

‘Taylor has signed here for a long time and he will stay here for a long time.

New signing Taylor Harwood-Bellis has been left out of Aston Villa's Champions League squad

Unai Emery admitted it was a 'hard decision' to omit the £30million signing from Southampton

🗣️ "To come to a club of the stature of Villa is something that I wanted to strive for."



Taylor's first words as a Villan – ready to kick-on 👊 pic.twitter.com/ryZzjvLAXS — Aston Villa (@AstonVilla) September 1, 2026

'Hopefully he will have chance to play in Europe with us, after January maybe but hopefully next year. As for Madjo, he is only 17 and will have more chances to play.’

Harwood-Bellis, who tied the knot with Roy Keane's daughter Leah earlier this summer, admitted he 'can't wait' to play in the Champions League during his first interview with his new club on Tuesday.

The defender said in a club video posted to X on Tuesday: 'I think when I knew first of all the club in general being such a prestigious Premier League club and then you have the added bonus of the Champions League is something that doesn't fill me with anything but excitement.

'I can't wait to get out there and show that I can hopefully do it on the biggest stage. We've seen the success the club's had in Europe, winning the Europa League and going so far in the Champions League, giving PSG probably their hardest game that season was massive.

'So yeah, I know that the club can relish in Europe and hopefully go a step further.'

While Harwood-Bellis is ineligible for Villa's league-phase campaign, which begins away to Club Brugge next Tuesday, he could still be added to the squad for the knockout stages if Emery's side progress.

Clubs who qualify for the knockouts are allowed to register a maximum of three additional players.

Harwood-Bellis tied the knot with Roy Keane's daughter Leah this summer (proposal pictured)

Aston Villa's Champions League squad in full: Zion Suzuki, Marco Bizot, Matteo Ruggeri, Victor Lindelof, Pau Torres, Boubacar Kamara, Joao Gomes, Leon Goretzka, John McGinn, Alysson, Ibrahim Mbaye, Emi Buendia, Johan Manzambi, Nciolas Jackson, Matty Cash, Aaron Wan-Bissaka, Ian Maatsen, Alejandro Garnacho, Tyrone Mings, Ross Barkley, Tammy Abraham, James Wright, Lamare Bogarde

Sports.title: Folarin Balogun is left OUT of Monaco's Conference League squad - just days after walking out on Everton deal at the last minute
Sports.content:
Folarin Balogun is left OUT of Monaco's Conference League squad - just days after walking out on Everton deal at the last minute

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Monaco forward Folarin Balogun has been left out of his side's squad for the Conference League after he chose not to join Everton at the 11th hour of deadline day.

Balogun had been set to sign for Everton, but issues arose with his medical, at which point Monaco agreed to sell midfielder Lamine Camara to Chelsea.

However, the Toffees then decided to proceed with the deal after renegotiating terms, meaning the Principality side pulled the plug on Camara's move to Stamford Bridge as they didn't want to lose both players.

Then, at the last moment, Balogun had a change of heart, meaning that he and Camara would stay at the Ligue 1 club, yet Chelsea were left furious by what had gone on.

Balogun's future is now uncertain – he could still leave the club to a team whose transfer window is still open – and it was thrown into more doubt when he was left out of Monaco's 25-man squad for the Conference League league phase.

As a result of the drama, Monaco chief Scuro held a press conference on Wednesday where he launched a staunch defence of his club and insisted that they were not 'the bad guys' in the scenario.

Folain Balogun has been left out of Monaco's Conference League squad just days after walking away from a move to Everton

Scuro explained how Monaco were happy to sell Balogun but were desperate to keep Camara, a position that had been communicated to the midfielder earlier on deadline day having rejected several approaches for him over the summer.

He said: 'During the day, we had a clear agreement for Balogun to go to Everton. Balogun flew yesterday morning to go for medicals and sign a contract.

'Balogun, besides the salary, was also an important source of income for the club. And then, Lamine would stay.

'This was what we had until mid-afternoon. What happened is that Chelsea were always testing and trying. What about Lamine? What about Lamine? I’ve been talking to them for the last 10 days.

'Around 4pm yesterday, we got a contact from Chelsea. "Okay, we sold a midfielder (Enzo Fernandez). Deal done. Is there any possibility that Monaco are open to selling Lamine?" The answer was the same. No, it’s not. At this moment, at 4pm, Balogun was in Liverpool undergoing his medical. Everything was going pretty well.'

Scuro added that at around 7pm, Everton then got in touch about issues with Balogun's medical, 'which for our medical staff, as well as the player's personal medical staff, made no sense at all'.

Although discussions continued with Everton over Balogun's physical health, Scuro explained that Chelsea then went again for Camara and a deal was discussed.

He added: 'And what happened was that around 10pm, maybe a bit earlier, Everton realised that, OK, there is no problem. We are ready to do it. Let’s sign the contract.

'As soon as we got the information, we came back to Chelsea and thought, "OK, we have our deal there. There is no deal on it (Camara)". Because it’s also fair to do this. It’s also part of the game.

'There is no reason that these kinds of dynamic discussions on the last day of the transfer window, which all of us decided to be on the last day, trying to find solutions, with the clock ticking, that this kind of interaction (sees us) become the bad guys in the room.

'Putting that on Monaco is not fair. So this is the story. We informed, again, everyone that there was no deal with Chelsea. We progressed (with Balogun).'

However, just as the deal was about to be completed, Balogun made the dramatic decision to not proceed with the move having been left upset by Everton's initial concerns surrounding his medical.

Scuro said: 'Balogun’s allegation is that "I’m not feeling good because of the way the club treated me. I’m not feeling good because Everton’s medical department raised doubts about my future or my health. I have nothing (no health problem), so I’m not comfortable signing a long contract here."

'And the reality is that when Balo mentioned to us this feeling that he was not comfortable, he didn’t want to sign. We didn’t see ourselves in a position to push him. We had to respect his decision.'

Scuro added that Balogun may still depart in the next few days to a league where the transfer window remains open, while he believes Camara could still move onto 'better things' in the future.

He also insisted he sympathised with both players over their respective sagas.

Sports.title: Refs turn on 'fantasy land' Mike Dean: Controversial ex-referee's colleagues and boss attack his 'minigames' claims which had fans calling for investigation into his behaviour
Sports.content:
Refs turn on 'fantasy land' Mike Dean: Controversial ex-referee's colleagues and boss attack his 'minigames' claims which had fans calling for investigation into his behaviour

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Mike Dean's former boss and colleagues have turned on the controversial ex-referee following claims he would play 'minigames' while officiating Premier League matches.

Former referees' chief Keith Hackett, fellow ex-top flight referee Graham Scott and referee body ProRef have all moved to rubbish the claims of Dean, who took charge of 553 Premier League games in his career.

'There used to be games we would have for a laugh,' Dean said on Jamie Vardy's Having a Party podcast. 'It would kick-off, right; see how long we could go without blowing a whistle.

'I done that a few times in the Premier League, before VAR, obviously. Went 20, 25 minutes without blowing the whistle.'

Dean continued: 'I used to do another one in the Premier League, I used to stand in the centre circle and see how long I could stay in the centre circle before I had to leave. That was just me joking about. Got about 15 minutes once, in one game.'

His comments have caused uproar in the football world, with fans questioning his integrity and former officials weighing in.

Past colleagues have turned on Mike Dean (pictured) after he admitted to sometimes trying to see how long he could go without blowing his whistle in a game

Dean's former refereeing boss Keith Hackett (pictured) has suggested there is no way the controversial ex-referee could have got away with minigames

Keith Hackett, who was a FIFA referee for more than two years and Dean's boss at PGMOL between 2004 and 2010, has looked to front that response.

Hackett wrote on X: 'Mike Dean is in fantasy land!! The examination of performances assessors is forensic. When I was boss referee's performances were forensically examined.

'Dean on my watch could not have done what he said with the monitoring systems in operation.'

Hackett added he was 'satisfied (Dean) is talking nonsense' and said: 'He clearly has damaged his reputation. The fallout does not help current refs.'

Scott, meanwhile, who refereed in the Premier League between 2015 and 2025, rubbished Dean's claims and argued that his behaviour post-retirement has been questionable.

'I worked with Mike loads of times - they're not true stories,' Scott said on talkSPORT. 'I wish people wouldn't do this kind of thing. It's the audio equivalent of clickbait, isn't it?

'It's to try and get people interested and laughing. It's palpable nonsense.'

He added: 'I found him quite shy, personally. I found him quite small when he was in a private situation.

Graham Scott, meanwhile, said Dean has shown 'precious little' common sense since retiring

Dean revealed his 'minigames' when speaking on Jamie Vardy's podcast, and his quotes have caused outrage

'What happened on the field, what happened in referee meetings, is he put on a persona that was way too far the other way, as a kind of coping mechanism.'

Scott also wrote in The Athletic: 'For all his common sense on the field, he has shown precious little of it since retiring. Casual comments that harm former colleagues and employers do not disappear when the following day's newspapers are thrown in the bin, yet hang around forever to cause untold damage to all referees' reputations.'

Daily Mail Sport understands Dean's comments have raised plenty of eyebrows within the current refereeing community too, with senior figures questioning the plausibility of his claim given the lack of detail.

According to senior officials at ProRef, Dean provided no indication of when these alleged 'minigames' took place. He also claimed they occurred before VAR was introduced for the 2019-20 season, meaning any such incidents would have taken place under previous refereeing chiefs – and current bosses are insistent that 'integrity and impartiality' are at the heart of referees' decision-making.

A number of fans, meanwhile, have taken to social media to voice their concern at Dean's suggestions.

One wrote: 'Why the f***'s he admitting to this? "Oooh look at me I ruined the integrity of top level football matches while getting paid a f***ing fortune for a laugh." And people wonder why we all think refs are *****.'

Dean has admitted, somewhat dismissively, that sometimes there was an element of wanting to be the 'centre of attention' when he was on the field.

'It's about wanting to be more a part of the game than what I should have been,' Dean said. 'If you play an advantage and it works off, you do celebrate it; if you get a decision right you kind of want to celebrate.

'I'd celebrate with the lads in my ear pieces and stuff. If you play an advantage and somebody scores, I think it's great. Love it.'

But despite his prior explanations to Vardy, whom he officiated several times while the striker played for Leicester, fans didn't find his declaration amusing.

Another fan added: '“Professional” referee by the way. This is something you would expect from a Sunday league keeper who’s earning pittance to get abused.

‘What an absolute f***ing ****. Always behaved like he was more important than the game being played around him.’

A different account wrote: 'How about, and I might be going out on a limb here, concentrating on officiating the matches properly rather than playing silly little games with yourself. Mike Dean thinking this makes him sound like a right lad is baffling to me.'

Sports.title: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua talks back ON to stage mega-fight at Wembley
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua talks back ON to stage mega-fight at Wembley

Talks regarding a fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua have hit a stumbling block, but promoter Eddie Hearn has dropped a major bombshell regarding the venue

View 2 Images Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua (Image: Getty Images)

Eddie Hearn has revealed that talks have now "reopened" to stage the showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua at Wembley Stadium.

‌



The pair agreed separate contracts to fight each other back in April - just days after Fury's comeback win over Arslanbek Makhmudov. Joshua's deal included the stipulation that the showcase must be held at Wembley in the UK. However, Netflix and the Saudi Arabian backers who are paying for the contest - which is pencilled in for November 20 - want it to be moved to New York.

‌



On Thursday afternoon, Fury had issued 'make or break' warning to Joshua and threatened to walk away from their all-British heavyweight dust-up. In the last few days, talks have hit a major stumbling block amid reports that the fight is set to be held Stateside.

‌



But Matchroom supremo Hearn took to social media on Friday afternoon - revealing that Wembley Stadium is being considered as the venue for the fight. He wrote: "I want to thank everyone for the unbelievable support! You have been heard and talks have now re-opened for Wembley. Let's make history with one of the biggest sporting moments (British flag) has ever seen."

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

Moses Itauma has stunning claim debunked after Filip Hrgovic loss READ MORE :

Recently, it emerged that the 'Gypsy King' would walk away from the contest if an agreement had not been made by the end of this week. And Fury doubled down on those claims after taking to social media and taking aim at both Joshua and Hearn in a scathing rant.

‌



In a video uploaded to Instagram, he said: "Quick update on what’s not happening. I am seeing Eddie (Hearn) doing a lot of interviews, trying to twist the narrative. The facts are… you do not want the fight. Because if you did, you would be ready to rock and roll like I am. Tyson Fury has already said a thousand times that he will fight anywhere. No problem at all.

"Banging on about England, but he moved to Monaco and the other freak's moved to Dubai. It’s not about England so much then is it boys? Turki has paid you tens of millions to fight and you are still acting like little b******. It is what it is. There is nothing I can do. I cannot make a coward fight. At the end of the day, you have shown your true colours. If AJ was any sort of man, he would overrule the sausage. And he would stand up and fight, but obviously he is not and that is where we are.

Moses Itauma told exactly what went wrong during Filip Hrgovic loss READ MORE :

"So, good luck to yous. And one thing for sure is, I won’t wait for a sausage who has been knocked spark out by Daniel Dubois. I have waited ten years for this and I have been ready every time. One thing I will not be doing is wasting my later years at 38 years old for a freak who does not want to fight. I will move on and there’s plenty of world champions out there who do want to fight and do want to make some money, so I will be giving them a knock. So there is plenty of men.

‌



"Agit Kabayel, Filip Hrgovic, Daniel Dubois - whoever else there is. They are all very brave men and they are all looking for a few quid. Maybe I will give them and a call and they can fight me in November because this is going nowhere. As always, ten years later, still in the same boat. Still nowhere. Still dragging on."

On Wednesday morning, promoter Frank Warren revealed to reporters, including Mirror Fighting, that Fury has signed the contract for the fight, while Joshua's signature remains overdue. "The latest is Joshua's not signed yet," he said.

View 2 Images Fury laid down the challenge at the start of April (Image: 2026 Mark Robinson)

‌



"It's not for me to give him [a deadline], it's the people who are paying the money. It's all this stuff, as I said from the beginning, it's about contracts. I know what the contracts say. The contracts have all got to be amended. And it's about people…

"Tyson's signed. Tyson's done. He don't care when the fight takes place. They want it in New York, they want it in Barbados, they want it on the Isle of Wight. He's signed. He's done.

"He signed for the fight in January. And the fight's supposed to take place in September, but what happened with AJ and his accident, that all got pushed back. And where we got to with it was obviously AJ had his fight back, late, and we'd already had that one in December with Jake Paul.

Article continues below

"Then he had another fight back with that MMA guy, struggled in that. And then, it was decided to put it on in November. But one contract says one venue, the other contract says another venue, and the TV contract says another venue."

Sports.title: Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe to be open to geldings from 2027 after major rule change
Sports.content:
Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe to be open to geldings from 2027 after major rule change

The decision means top middle distance horses such as Calandagan will be eligible to run in the 2027 edition if he remains in training following the ruling by the European Pattern Committee

View 3 Images The Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe had been restricted to entire male and female horses since its creation (Image: Getty Images)

Next year's Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe will be open to geldings for the first time after the European Pattern Committee gave the green light to a ground-breaking proposal from France Galop.

‌



The decision marks a landmark shift for Europe's most prestigious middle-distance race which takes place on the first Sunday in October each year.

‌



The ParisLongchamp race draws some of the best horses from around the world yet the contest has been closed to high profile geldings like Francis-Henri Graffard's King George winner Goliath and Calandagan, ranked the best horse in the world in 2025 after winning the King George, Champion Stakes and Japan Cup.

‌



Top trainers Alan King and Lucinda Russell 'named' by government for underpaying workers READ MORE :

The decision was made during a meeting of the European Patter Committee in Berlin on Friday, attended by representatives from Britain, France, Ireland and Germany. Members voted through the change after a presentation by France Galop who said it would help to improve the popularity of the race as an international contest.

France Galop president Guillaume de Saint-Seine said: "The European Pattern Committee's decision is an important milestone in the consultation and decision-making process initiated by France Galop.

"The EPC's support confirms the soundness of our approach. Opening the Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe to geldings is driven by a straightforward objective: to ensure that France's greatest race brings together the best horses – colts, fillies and, from 2027, geldings.

‌



View 3 Images Calandagan, named best racehorse in the world in 2025, would be eligible to run in the 2027 Arc (Image: PA)

"We are convinced that this change will make the race even more compelling on the track and further strengthen its international profile and media appeal."

Major racing figures had already voiced their objection to the proposal when first announced.

‌



Speaking earlier in the summer Coolmore boss John Magnier said: "I hope they don't let the geldings into the Arc. I think most of the purists would be against it.

"There are two sides to every coin, but I'm only giving it from the breeding side and from the breed as a whole. The Arc is one of the real races and it won't be any more if you include geldings.

View 3 Images John Magnier opposed the change

Article continues below

"My father-in-law (Vincent O'Brien) used to always say that if he was training a yard of geldings the bookmakers would be in worse trouble!".

Record eight-time Arc winner said in June: "I am firmly against it – I cannot see any benefit. It is true that the last few winners have not gone on to be successful stallions, apart from Sea The Stars (2009), but we need more stallions not less.

"The Arc is always a big field so that is not the reason and will agree that a gelding is much easier to train than a colt – it is an advantage. I'm a big fan of tradition and do not like to break it without a serious reason. Just because there are one or two horses horses who are better gelded, it would be a shame."

Sports.title: Top trainers Alan King and Lucinda Russell 'named' by government for underpaying workers
Sports.content:
Top trainers Alan King and Lucinda Russell 'named' by government for underpaying workers

King, who has apologised, and Russell appeared on a list of more than 600 British employers who owed money to staff having failed to pay the minimum wage

View 3 Images Alan King and Lucinda Russell: appeared on the government's list (Image: Getty Images)

Top trainers Alan King and Lucinda Russell have been named by the government for underpaying their workers.

‌



Dual purpose trainer King, who last month captured the Ebor Handicap at York with Daiquiri Bay, and two-time Grand National winner Russell were included on a list of employers who had failed to pay the minimum wage.

‌



The list has been regularly published since 2011 in an effort to hold bosses to account and make sure improvements are made as quickly as possible when pay is owed to staff. In the latest publication Alan King Racing Limited is reported to have failed to pay £19,050.72 to 24 workers, putting him 36th on the list of more than 600 employers

‌



Trainer Mickey Bowen announces move to RoseWill Stables purchased by private investor READ MORE :

Miss Lucinda V Russell, trading as Arlary House Stables, failed to pay £2,158.39 to two workers. She was 323 on the list.

Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said: “The best businesses know that looking after your workers isn’t just the right thing to do, it’s the smart thing to do, building the stronger, more successful businesses that drive growth in every postcode.

“Most employers already understand this, and I want to work with them to ensure they have every piece of guidance and support available to help them follow the rules. Short-changing your staff isn’t a shortcut to success and we are determined to stamp it out.”

‌



View 3 Images Daiquiri Bay (number 8) was the narrow winner of the Ebor in August (Image: Getty Images)

The national living wage and national minimum wage rates are £12.71 per hour for adults aged 21 or over, £10.85 per hour for those aged 18 to 20, and £8 per hour for under 18s and apprentices.

King, a multiple Cheltenham Festival-winning trainer, apologised for not making the correct payments.

‌



He told the Racing Post: “We sincerely apologise to our colleagues who were affected by these past administrative errors. Our employees are the backbone of the business, and they deserve to be compensated accurately.

View 3 Images Lucinda Russell with Grand National winner Corach Rambler (Image: PA)

“As soon as HMRC brought this to our attention, we co-operated fully and all affected employees were back-paid on conclusion in 2023. HMRC identified a technical underpayment for 24 employees, totalling £19,050.72 – this represented a small fraction of under one per cent of total payroll in the review period.

Article continues below

“The regulations surrounding National Minimum Wage can be complicated, but that is not an excuse. We have learned from this process and are fully confident that our current operations prevent any repeat of these issues.”

Russell said: “It was two errors as opposed to intentionally doing so regularly. We take the payment of staff very seriously and pay over the minimum wage. When they looked into the payment of all the other staff, of which we have around 60, they were all happy with them.”

Sports.title: Roy Keane's £25m son-in-law Taylor Harwood-Bellis dealt crushing Aston Villa blow
Sports.content:
Roy Keane's £25m son-in-law Taylor Harwood-Bellis dealt crushing Aston Villa blow

Taylor Harwood-Bellis joined Aston Villa from Southampton on transfer deadline day but the £25million defender has NOT been registered in their Champions League squad

View 2 Images Aston Villa new boy Taylor Harwood-Bellis has not been included in their Champions League squad (Image: Matt Watson/Southampton FC via Getty Images)

Taylor Harwood-Bellis has been omitted from Aston Villa's 23-man Champions League squad - just days after moving to Villa Park.

‌



The central defender, 24, completed a protracted £25million switch from Southampton to Villa on transfer deadline day following weeks of speculation over a move away. Harwood-Bellis' arrival strengthens Villa's defence after they reluctantly sanctioned the sale of Ezri Konsa to Arsenal last month.

‌



Harwood-Bellis could make his Premier League debut for Villa this weekend when they travel to Hull - but it's a different story when it comes to Europe.

‌



Due to only having two “club-trained” players, Villa are only permitted to name a 23-man 'A list' squad rather than the usual 25 limit. And Harwood-Bellis is one of the unlucky ones who has failed to make the cut.

He is the only summer signing not to be registered, with Zion Suzuki, Matteo Ruggeri, Aaron Wan-Bissaka, Leon Goretzka, Joao Gomes, Johan Manzambi, Nicolas Jackson, Alejandro Garnacho and Ibahim Mbaye all in the squad.

‌



Harwood-Bellis' move to Villa Park descended into a bit of a saga during the final weeks of the window with Villa initially failing to meet Southampton's valuation for the defender, who represented England back in 2024. The Saints were almost promoted to the Premier League themselves last season, reaching the final of the Championship play-offs before being expelled over 'Spygate'.

Roy Keane, Harwood-Bellis' father-in-law, alluded to some of the difficulties of the situation behind the scenes and lauded the former Saints player's professionalism during the situation, telling the The Overlap: “He is a lot more professional than I was.

View 2 Images Roy Keane spoke about Harwood-Bellis on a recent edition of The Overlap (Image: The Overlap / YouTube)

‌



“Really good kid. He has a lot of ups and downs as any footballers do and waiting for the deal to go through.

“He does not speak to me much about it. I have boundaries with him and I won’t be interfering with his business. Every now and again you might just give a bit of advice but not I would not be overbearing. He has his own stuff to do.”

The former Manchester United and Ireland midfielder added: “That last year as [Southampton] were kicked out of the play-offs I think Villa is a great move for him.”

Sports.title: Michael Carrick hints Man Utd fell short in transfer window and opens up on budget
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick hints Man Utd fell short in transfer window and opens up on budget

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick feels his side have made the most of the finances they had available to them this summer

View 2 Images Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has been speaking about the transfer window (Image: 2026 Manchester United FC Getty Images)

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has hinted that his side fell just short in the transfer market despite the arrivals of Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba, Tynan Thompson, Kit Margeson, Cristian Orozco and Karl Darlow. United strengthened their midfield but were linked with a new left-back throughout the summer, choosing not to sign one before the summer transfer deadline passed.

‌



Carrick is largely pleased with the business his side has done, spending £152m - though Swansea were paid compensation for Margeson and Orozco arrived for an undisclosed fee, which would bump that up further. The Red Devils were also linked with a move for another striker in the transfer window, but will have to wait until January to bolster Carrick's squad further.

‌



Speaking at his pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon, Carrick said: "We went into the window wanting to come out stronger. From the group we had last season. We’ve added to that, we’ve done a lot of good work.

‌



"The situation is what it is in terms of finances and what we can work with. The players we brought in, I’m delighted with, for the quality and level we’ve got, I’m really happy with.

Marcus Rashford gets new Man Utd tattoo on Old Trafford return after 18 months away READ MORE :

"There is always other things you can do or could have done, that’s part of evolving the group and trying to push all the time. We had certain things we needed to fill, try and improve the group, and largely I think we’re in a good group.

"We have a good dynamic in the squad. We’ve got players that are flexible in the team and can play in different positions. Largely pretty happy."

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"What squad is ever perfect?" Carrick added. "You always have to find ways of adapting. When you’re building and going through a period where we’re trying to get to the top, you have to make steps.

"It’s not going to be one hit. Not just talking about players, it’s the whole thing, improving as a group, as a squad. It’s not an instant fix.

‌



View 2 Images Joshua Zirkzee had been expected to leave United but stayed put (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

"There’s a whole road we have to go down with that and make sure we keep improving and in the end we want to be going where we want to be. There’s always things that we’re looking at and trying to improve."

Joshua Zirkzee was one of the players linked with a move away from Old Trafford, but he stayed at United and Carrick still sees him as an important member of the squad.

‌



"Josh is important," the United boss said It’s the team, the squad, the depth for the whole season. Josh is happy here, I have a really good relationship with him. He wants to play more than he has done.

"That’s the healthy competition for places. We have a lot of games coming up and a shorter period between games. Josh can do some really top things. I’ve seen it myself and I look forward to him doing it a little bit more."
