World.title: Industrial production up by 2.3% in July, led by wood and machinery
World.content:
Total industrial production rose by 2.3 percent at constant prices year‑on‑year in July, Statistics Estonia reported, with growth across all three sectors.

Output increased by 13.5 percent in mining, 16 percent in energy production and 1.1 percent in manufacturing, which had declined for five consecutive months before July.

Commenting on the results, Riin Kadarik, leading analyst at Statistics Estonia, said manufacturing was boosted by the manufacture of wood, the biggest manufacturing industry, where output increased by 10.8 percent compared with July last year. "Nearly half of the increase in output in this activity was contributed by the manufacture of solid fuels from vegetable biomass," Kadarik said.

Industrial production changes. Source: Statistics Estonia

There was also significant growth in the manufacture of machinery and equipment, where output grew by 30.3 percent, mainly due to the production of lifting equipment and special‑purpose machinery. Output increased in two‑thirds of manufacturing activities, with food production growing by 1.5 percent — its first increase since December 2025.

Of the major activities, the manufacture of fabricated metal products saw a fall in output for the second consecutive month, dropping by 0.9 percent in July.

Compared with June, seasonally adjusted total industrial production rose by 0.9 percent, with manufacturing up 0.2 percent.

In July, 65.2 percent of manufacturing production was sold to the external market. Compared with July 2025, sales of manufacturing production increased by 7.9 percent at current prices, with domestic sales up 8.6 percent and export sales up 7.5 percent.

Volume index and its trend. Source: Statistics Estonia

Energy production rose by 16 percent in July, with electricity production increasing by 9.6 percent and heat production by 13.2 percent year‑on‑year. "The increase in electricity production in July was mainly due to greater domestic production, as imports remained similar to last year's level," Kadarik said.

Statistics Estonia compiled the data on behalf of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications.

More detailed information is available from Statistics Estonia's website here, here and here.

World.title: Iraqi judiciary completes interrogation of 5,700 ISIS suspects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Supreme Judicial Council of Iraq has officially concluded the interrogation process for 5,704 ISIS detainees who were moved from northeastern Syria earlier this year, preparing them for trial.

The First Karkh Investigation Court said in a statement on Tuesday that it concluded the investigation phase of one of Iraq’s largest terrorism-related cases in history.

The verified detainees originate from 67 different nationalities, including 3,497 Syrians and 474 Iraqis.

The courts identified very dangerous agents in key leadership, military, financial, media, and security roles inside ISIS.

Six offenders were actively linked to the captivity, detention, transfer, sale, and exploitation of Yazidi women, exposing serious international crimes.

Several suspects have previously been cleared and released due to insufficient evidence linking them to terrorism crimes.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate rises in Baghdad, remain stable in Erbil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in Baghdad, the Iraqi capital, and remained stable in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,547.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,546.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad rose, ranging between 1,552.5 Iraqi dinars and 1,542.5 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate remained stable, fluctuating between 1,546 and 1,545.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation represented more than a 10 percent difference in exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq exports fuel oil through Jordan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told Attaqa News that Iraq began exporting fuel oil shipments via Jordan for the first time last month.

Al-Rikabi explained that Iraq is exporting fuel oil through the neighboring country, not to Jordan.

The Iraqi official did not disclose the details of the agreement, its duration, or when it came into effect.

Iraqi oil shipments started flowing to Jordan in early August through the Trebil border crossing, the only land border crossing between the two countries, at a rate of 10,000 barrels per day, which were stored in the facilities of the Jordan Oil Terminals Company (JOTC), Jordan’s state-owned petroleum logistics and independent storage provider.

Through Jordan, a shipment totaling 307,000 barrels was exported to Greece.

Following the Strait of Hormuz crisis, which began with the United States’ war against Iran on February 28, Iraqi fuel oil shipments began transiting through Syria via tanker trucks, with storage at the Baniyas refinery before shipping to worldwide markets.

Between March and the end of August, Iraq exported 21.4 million barrels of fuel oil through Syria and only 307,000 barrels through Jordan.

Iraqi fuel oil exports started to increase following the Middle East conflict until the end of August in an attempt to compensate for the declining supplies via the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: 38 officers, 3,000 personnel dismissed over corruption in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Interior announced on Thursday that it permanently dismissed 38 officers and 180 personnel over administrative and financial corruption, with another 3,245 personnel discharged for desertion.

The purge represents a significant internal effort as part of the ongoing “Operation Dawn,” a nationwide anti-corruption campaign spearheaded by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government. The campaign has targeted numerous public officials and high-profile individuals.

According to an official statement from Miqdad Miri, the spokesperson for the Interior Ministry, the total number of individuals affected encompasses various categories of misconduct.

After receiving clear evidence of their direct involvement in bribery and financial misconduct, 38 officers were permanently removed from service.

Finalized judicial verdicts convicting 180 enlisted personnel of corruption accusations resulted in their official removal from service.

As part of larger ministry attempts to reestablish strong institutional discipline, 3,245 service personnel were discharged only for abandoning their duties.

These dismissals took place within the first 100 days of the current government’s tenure.

This security-sector cleanup is part of the larger nationwide drive “Operation Dawn.” Between late June and August, security operations resulted in the arrest of at least 210 lawmakers, public servants, and business executives.

World.title: Iraq, AIIB discuss financing development projects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Finance Minister Faleh Sari met with a delegation from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) led by Konstantin Limitovskiy on Wednesday to discuss funding infrastructure and development projects in Iraq.

During their meeting in Baghdad, the AIIB delegation reviewed its global and regional portfolios to outline how its framework will apply to Iraq across the transportation, energy, water, and digital infrastructure sectors, according to a statement cited by the Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The discussions focused on the Development Road Project, Iraq’s mega-highway and rail corridor intended to connect the Gulf to Europe.

The AIIB publicly stated its willingness to fund and assist this important trans-regional corridor, acknowledging its enormous potential to drive economic diversification.

The Iraqi Ministry of Transport held separate discussions with the World Bank and the AIIB to determine the technological integrations necessary for the project’s ports and rail networks.

The AIIB delegation expressed its willingness to assist and fund important projects in Iraq, particularly major infrastructure projects, such as the Development Road project, which would boost the country’s economic development.

World.title: Iraq launches plan to recover 100,000 artifacts smuggled abroad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has launched a comprehensive plan to recover over 100,000 artifacts that were unearthed through illegal excavation and smuggled out of the country.

The Iraqi Ministry of Culture, Tourism, and Antiquities announced a broad endeavor to recover the country’s stolen Mesopotamian heritage using a combination of cultural diplomacy, security surveillance, and strong legal action.

The ministry’s undersecretary, Qasim al-Sudani, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the government’s agenda prioritizes the tourism sector.

The strategy emphasizes recovering documented items that were assigned official museum inventory numbers prior to their theft and smuggling, especially during the tumultuous period following the 2003 US-led invasion.

The initiative also seeks to tackle the significant number of unrecorded artifacts found during illegal and random excavations.

Since these items lack formal records, they pose a substantially more difficult legal issue to monitor and authenticate.

The Iraqi government has formed a combined domestic task force comprising the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Interior, the National Intelligence Service, and the National Security Service to carry out the plan.

Security agencies are cooperating with Iraqi embassies to identify stolen treasures that appear at public or private auctions abroad.

While countries like the United Kingdom and the United States have actively assisted in the return of tens of thousands of artifacts, Iraqi officials have indicated that some nations have intentionally delayed the repatriation process.

Iraq is also taking legal actions internationally against foreign businesses or individuals who are keeping Iraqi artifacts.

World.title: Iraq evaluates exploration blocks to optimize gas output
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil is actively assessing its exploration blocks and foreign alliances to maximize domestic gas output.

Director of the state-owned Midland Oil Company (MOC), Mohammed Yassin Hassan, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the ministry is focusing on unexploited exploration areas rather than existing resources.

The strategic measure seeks to attract multinational corporations to invest in Iraq’s growing natural gas sector.

Instead of altering production at current sites, the Oil Ministry is focusing on new exploration regions to identify new deposits.

Due to the strong interest in Iraq’s untapped energy potential, multinational energy businesses have already begun contacting the ministry.

Iraq’s MOC is actively pursuing partnerships with major US firms, such as ConocoPhillips, to lead gas development projects in important areas in the provinces of Diyala and Anbar.

Expanding operations in blocks such as the Akkas and Mansuriya gas fields is critical to Iraq’s long-term strategy for achieving energy independence and providing the necessary fuel for power plants to generate electricity.

World.title: Marsoumi: Iraq’s 10M bpd oil goal faces $75B cost and OPEC+ hurdles
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s strategic plan to scale crude oil production to 10 million barrels per day (bpd) by 2030 faces formidable structural, financial, and geopolitical hurdles, prominent Iraqi economic analyst Dr. Nabil Al-Marsoumi warned on Wednesday, September 2, 2026.

The assessment follows directives issued on Tuesday by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, who instructed the Ministry of Oil to expand exploration licensing rounds and ramp up extraction across fields in federal territory and the Kurdistan Region to target nearly 10 million bpd over the next four years.

Al-Marsoumi outlined four primary structural constraints standing between Iraq’s current production baseline and the 10-million-bpd horizon:

OPEC+ Baseline & Quota Negotiation: Iraq currently produces approximately 4.431 million bpd against an OPEC+ baseline allocation of 4.651 million bpd. Pushing production toward 10 million bpd requires formal revision of Iraq’s sovereign quota—a concession requiring consensus among major OPEC+ members.

Sustainable Capacity Ceiling: US petroleum consultancy DeGolyer and MacNaughton is actively auditing the maximum sustainable capacity across 19 OPEC+ nations. Preliminary assessments project Iraq’s sustainable 12-month ceiling at 5.0 to 5.5 million bpd, revealing a 4.5-million-bpd capacity deficit below the 2030 target.

Capital Expenditure Threshold ($75 Billion): Based on global industry benchmarks averaging $15 billion in capital investment per 1 million bpd of added capacity, Iraq must mobilize roughly $75 billion in upstream and midstream funding. This capital must finance seawater treatment and injection facilities, storage farm expansions, pumping stations, and new maritime and northern pipeline export corridors.

Price Collapse & Market Saturation Risks: Global oil absorption capacity remains constrained by demand growth projections. Injecting millions of additional Iraqi barrels risks igniting a market-share price war among producers, which could trigger a global oil price collapse harmful to Baghdad’s hydrocarbon-dependent treasury.

Comparative Analysis: Current Capacity vs. 2030 Target

Metric / Parameter Current Level (2026) 2030 Government Target Gap / Required Expansion Crude Output ~4.431 Million bpd 10.000 Million bpd +5.569 Million bpd Sustainable Ceiling 5.0 – 5.5 Million bpd 10.000 Million bpd +4.500 Million bpd OPEC+ Production Baseline 4.651 Million bpd Revised Allocation Required Requires OPEC+ Consensus Estimated Capital Outlay Baseline operational budget ~$75 Billion cumulative $15B per 1M bpd capacity Export Infrastructure Constrained southern/northern routes New northern & deepwater sea lines Major pipeline & storage expansion

Al-Marsoumi cautioned that upstream expansion cannot occur in isolation from global energy market fundamentals. Without substantial foreign direct investment to finance water injection schemes and deepwater export berths, aggressive target-setting risks outpacing actual midstream logistics.

Furthermore, aggressively pursuing volume over price discipline could depress international crude benchmarks, reducing net state oil revenues even as export volumes increase.

World.title: Dog bite ordeal doesn’t end with rabies prophylaxis
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: For a 21-year-old Delhi resident bitten by a stray dog, the ordeal did not end after he received rabies post-exposure prophylaxis. Within seven days, he developed a skin rash that progressed to severe hives (urticaria) and angioedema, causing sudden swelling of the face, lips and throat. His condition later worsened with breathing difficulty, requiring specialist dermatological intervention.The case comes against the backdrop of the Supreme Courtâs May 2026 directions on the stray-dog menace, which stressed the need to protect people from dog attacks and strengthen measures for sterilisation, vaccination and dog-bite management.The young man was bitten over two weeks ago and was initially taken to a Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) centre, where he received equine immunoglobulin (IgG) and a rabies vaccine.He was later taken to Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital. After two days of treatment, when he developed difficulty breathing, he was evaluated by the dermatology department.Doctors advised a single injection of omalizumab to control the severe allergic reaction. The medicine cost around Rs 16,000-17,000. The family was advised to explore obtaining it through the Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS), but the patientâs mother, Rama (name changed), bought it herself, worried about her sonâs condition.The patient improved within 24 hours of receiving omalizumab and remains under treatment at RML Hospital.Dr Kabir Sardana, who treated the patient in the dermatology department, said he sees around one such case a week and believes this could be the first reported use of omalizumab for this type of reaction following rabies prophylaxis. The treatment was given after the option was discussed with the family and with their concurrence.Sardana said it can sometimes be difficult to distinguish whether a rash is due to the vaccine or immunoglobulin, as both early and delayed reactions can occur. âThe aim is to maximise treatment, minimise discomfort and, of course, see the financial aspects of the patient,â he said.The episode also highlighted the financial burden of managing severe reactions. âEvery patient cannot afford Rs 17,000. What can poor people do? They are suffering so much,â Rama said.More broadly, he said, adverse reactions following rabies post-exposure prophylaxis can be difficult to predict and may be under-reported, particularly skin reactions. Doctors are concerned that severe reactions could create fear of rabies injections and prompt some people to delay or avoid prophylaxis.Doctors stress, however, that people bitten or scratched by a potentially rabid animal should not avoid recommended post-exposure prophylaxis. Patients should instead be counselled about possible reactions and have timely access to medical care if serious symptoms develop.The concern is greater in rural and poorly resourced areas, where access to specialist and emergency care may be limited. Doctors say the case underlines the need for better reporting of adverse reactions and timely access to treatment when complications occur.

World.title: Bargaining tactics? Why BJP's 'solo pitch' in Punjab may have message for Akalis
World.content:
Is the BJP playing hardball with the Akalis in

? Yet another senior BJP leader has announced that the party will contest all 117 assembly seats in Punjab on its own strength.

BJP national general secretary Satish Poonia, in his first media interaction after being appointed the party's organisational in-charge for Punjab, made it clear that the message from the central leadership was to prepare for all 117 constituencies in the state.

He also sought to play down Shiromani Akali Dal chief Sukhbir Singh Badal's meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi last month, saying meetings between political leaders should not automatically be read as signs of an alliance.

Poonia is not the first senior BJP leader to reiterate the 'solo contest' point.

BJP national general secretary (organisation) BL Santosh had earlier told party functionaries in Punjab that the BJP would contest all 117 assembly seats independently.

BJP national general secretary (organisation) BL Santosh reiterated that the party is preparing to contest all 117 Punjab assembly seats.

And yet, the speculation of an alliance between the two parties refuses to go away.

The question then is whether the BJP is really shutting the door on its old ally or raising the bar before any possible deal.

BJP's message: We can do it alone

The BJP today has reasons to sound more confident than it did when both parties went their separate ways.

The BJP in Punjab was the junior partner of the Akalis for decades. The arrangement gave the BJP a share of Punjab's urban and Hindu-dominated constituencies while the SAD remained the dominant force in the alliance.





In the 2017 assembly election, the last Punjab polls the two parties contested together, the SAD fought 94 seats and the BJP just 23. The BJP won three and the Akalis 15.

This arrangement will clearly no longer work for the BJP.

Since splitting with the Akalis, the BJP has been working towards a plan. The party has been trying to expand beyond its old pockets in Punjab, in line with its national growth, and build an independent base.

The West Bengal victory has indeed strengthened the confidence within the party. Punjab BJP leaders have also publicly argued that the party's improved vote share and national presence have strengthened the case for fighting the elections independently.

That makes the repeated declaration of contesting 117 seats more than just a message to the Akalis. It is also a message to BJP workers that the party intends to build its own organisation across Punjab.

But the doors don't seem completely shut

Interestingly, even in the middle of this high-pitched rhetoric, the Student Organisation of India (SOI), which is the studentsâ wing of the Shiromani Akali Dal, extended support to the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) candidate in the Panjab University Campus Studentsâ Council elections and helped its candidate win the presidential post.

The SOI offered this olive branch to BJPâs student wing a day before the voting and helped ABVP create a record of winning the top post in the studentsâ council election for the second time in a row.

This campus politics bonhomie was significant messaging. The Akalis, who had walked away from the decades-old alliance with the BJP in 2020 over the now-repealed farm bills, have dropped very clear and open hints that they desperately want to revive the ties.

There have been a series of overtures from their end to seek an alliance without expressing that in as many words.

Akalis have not been subtle about wanting alliance with BJP

If the BJP is keeping its cards close to its chest, the Akalis have been far more open about it.

The PM Modi-Sukhbir Badal meeting was perhaps the beginning of this outreach. It was their first one-on-one political meeting since the SAD walked out of the BJP-led NDA in 2020 over the three farm laws, ending an alliance that had lasted nearly two decades.

Days after this meeting, the SAD reversed its stand on the Delimitation Bill and announced its support for the constitutional amendment bill which the BJP is trying to pass in Parliament.

This was a huge U-turn that prompted digs from the ruling AAP and the Congress over the SADâs desperation for an alliance with the BJP.

The shift in stance drew attention because the party had earlier taken a much more critical position on delimitation. The SAD had in April stated in Lok Sabha that the BJP was repeatedly changing the goal post on women's reservation and decried that the delimitation exercise was being conducted in the garb of the Women's Reservation Bill.

Then came more signals from within the Akali leadership.

Senior Akali leader Bikram Singh Majithia went public advocating an alliance, and said that people want SAD and the BJP to come together for peace, development and progress of Punjab.

Majithia's statement came after his sister and former Union minister Harsimrat Kaur Badal stoked fresh speculation about a re-alliance between the Akali Dal and the BJP by expressing a cryptic wish for "agreements" that carried progress to Punjab from Delhi.

Former Union minister Harsimrat Kaur Badal's remarks added to speculation over a possible revival of ties.

None of these statements amounted to a formal alliance proposal. However, they made it clear that the Akali leadership was increasingly interested in reviving ties with the BJP.

Akalis need BJP more than before

The reason is not difficult to see. The Akalis have been pushed to the fringes of Punjab politics.

Its vote share and seat share have declined in the last few elections. In fact, in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP managed a huge lead over SAD in terms of vote share.

The BJP secured 18.56% of the votes but failed to win a parliamentary seat in Punjab. The Akali Dal, despite winning Bathinda, finished with 13.42% vote share.

The BJP also finished ahead of SAD candidates across several constituencies and led in 24 assembly segments. In the 2022 assembly polls, by comparison, the BJP's vote share was only around 6.6%, while SAD was a little over 18%.

That perhaps explains why the Akalis seem desperate for an alliance.

Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann has claimed that the Shiromani Akali Dal leadership is "on its knees" to forge an alliance with the BJP and return to power in the state to "loot" it again.

Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann accused the Akali Dal of seeking a reunion with the BJP for political power.

So, the big question is: why is the BJP acting tough? Is it against reviving the alliance with the Akalis? Or is the BJP just playing hardball to ensure that it is the âbig brotherâ in any future alliance?

For the Akalis, the decline has been much more painful.

Akalis, who dominated Punjab politics for years, were reduced to three seats in the 2022 assembly election and one Lok Sabha seat in 2024. Now, the party has to compete not only with the Congress but also with AAP, which swept the last state election, and also a BJP trying to expand independently.

That perhaps explains the urgency.

Why BJP may have kept the door open

When BJP and SAD were in alliance earlier, there was little ambiguity about who was the senior partner.

The SAD had more seats and more say in deciding the assembly seats and the chief ministerial candidate. The BJP accepted most terms because the arrangement perhaps gave the BJP a space where its independent visibility was limited.

But now, if there is an alliance between the two again, it surely will be on completely different terms.

The BJP has spent the years since the split trying to build an identity of its own in Punjab.

It has brought leaders from other parties into its fold, expanded its organisation and fielded candidates across the entire state in the 2024 Lok Sabha election.

Even in recent weeks, it has continued inducting figures from outside the party as it prepares for the assembly contest.

For the BJP, therefore, returning to an arrangement in which it simply receives around 20-odd seats would be difficult. This is perhaps where the bargaining may be happening.

Therefore, the real question might just be if the Akalis are willing to accept the changed political reality.

There is another reason why the BJP may be keeping the Akalis guessing.

Declaring an alliance too early could derail BJP's bid to strengthen its organisation in the state build an independent identity. Keeping the 117-seat option alive allows the BJP to continue expanding and encouraging its cadres.

The BJP knows the Akalis are willing to return. There is little reason for the BJP to make any commitment before discussing seats and leadership.

The public posturing notwithstanding, the BJP also stands to gain from a possible alliance. The BJP's 18.56% vote share in the Lok Sabha election did not translate into a single seat. This shows that the party did expand its base, but that vote share by itself may not be enough.

The Akalis, meanwhile, still have traditional pockets of support. That gives both sides something the other may want.

But does BJP actually need the Akalis?

Fighting independently gives it the freedom to contest every region, develop new leaders and try to move beyond its traditional urban base.

Even an election in which it improves substantially without forming the government could further that objective. An alliance with SAD could interrupt that process.

Also, the Sikh community's identity continues to play an important role in Punjab politics. For the BJP, a renewed alliance with the Akali Dal could help it reach sections of Sikh voters and rural Punjab where the party has traditionally struggled to build a strong independent base.

For now, the two sides appear to be speaking in very different registers.

The Akalis have repeatedly sent signals that they are willing to reopen the relationship. The BJP is listening but not reacting. For now, all BJP leaders are maintaining that the party is preparing for all 117 seats.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Yet the Modi-Sukhbir meeting, the SOI-ABVP cooperation and reports of discussions behind the scenes mean the possibility of an alliance cannot be written off either.

It is possible that the BJP means exactly what it says and will go into the election alone. But if the two former allies do eventually come together, it is unlikely to be a return to the partnership that existed before 2020.

The fight, therefore, may not just be about whether BJP and SAD become allies again. It may be about who gets to be the 'big brother' this time.

World.title: 'We will formulate plan': Ram Temple's first CEO Jeetendra Mishra after Ayodhya trip
World.content:
Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra (retd) on Friday said the responsibility of the Ram temple was now on his shoulders after taking charge as the first chief executive officer (CEO) of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust.

âI have now taken charge as the CEO. The responsibility (of the Ram temple) has now come onto my shoulders,â Mishra told PTI Videos before leaving for Delhi after his two-day visit to

.

Mishra, who headed the Western Air Command during Operation Sindoor, was appointed the first CEO of the temple trust on Wednesday.

The trust also appointed Govind Dev Giri as general secretary, Mahesh Bhagchandka as treasurer, and inducted Madan Mohan Pandey and Nirmala Yadav as trustees.

First visit focused on understanding temple operations

During his first visit to Ayodhya as the trust's CEO, Mishra said his immediate focus was on familiarising himself with the functioning of the temple and the trust.

âI have only been here for one day, so this was a preliminary introductory visit. I will come here again after two or three days,â he said.

âThis was an introductory visit, during which I got an introduction to the functioning of the temple. Gradually, as I learn more about it, we will formulate some plans,â he added.





Mishra also said he would move forward with the guidance and cooperation of the trust once he had gained a better understanding of the entire system.

He said, âRight now I am trying to learn about the entire system myself. Once I understand everything, I will take orders and guidance from the Trust. With the cooperation of our team, we will move forward.â

During his visit, trust members briefed Mishra on its administrative and financial operations, including accounting procedures.

He also held meetings with members and office-bearers and inquired about the functioning of both the trust and the temple.

Selected after 5,585 applications

The 62-year-old retired as head of the Western Air Command on April 30. He was selected from a shortlist of three candidates after 5,585 applications were received for the post.

Mishra has 39 years of experience in various branches of the Indian Air Force and has been awarded the Uttam Yuddh Seva Medal.

He had earlier described himself as âthe most fortunate personâ to have been given vital responsibilities twice in his life, once to serve the nation and now to serve Lord Ram and his devotees.

âI consider myself the most fortunate person today to have been given vital responsibilities twice in my life -- once for national service and now for the organisation and administration of Shri Ram's temple and for Shri Ram's devotees,â he had said.

Administrative overhaul at Ram temple trust

Mishra's appointment comes amid a wider administrative overhaul by the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust following the controversy over alleged embezzlement of temple donations, which led to the arrest of eight people and the resignation of Champat Rai as its general secretary.

World.title: 'Thank you, dear PM Modi': Meloni signals deepening India-Italy strategic embrace
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni on Friday thanked Prime Minister

for congratulating her on becoming Italyâs longest continuously serving PM in the postwar period, saying the relationship between the two countries was âstronger than everâ.

Sharing a post on X, Meloni said, âThank you, dear Narendra Modi, for your words and for your friendship. The relationship between Italy and India is today stronger than ever.â

âThe Special Strategic Partnership that we launched during our last meeting is the recognition of the importance of this bond and of the will to unite the expertise of our Nations to create new opportunities for growth, seizing the extraordinary opportunities for collaboration that we have before us,â she said.

World.title: Karnataka embarks on cloud seeding as dry spell threatens to worsen
World.content:
Amid drought conditions, the Karnataka government on Friday launched a cloud-seeding programme in the hope of triggering rainfall in areas facing a severe rain deficit.

The programme was flagged off at the HAL airport by Water Resources Minister N. Cheluvarayaswamy, according to a government communiqué. A specially equipped light aircraft will be used for cloud-seeding operations, and the project is estimated to cost ₹28.52 crore.

The Minister admitted that a cloud-seeding operation undertaken earlier had a success rate of only 35%. However, he said every effort to augment water availability was important in the face of a worsening drought situation.

Success rate

He said the State had received very little rainfall this year and that the southwest monsoon would conclude by the end of this month.

“If adequate drinking water is not stored by the end of this month, there will be severe scarcity until the end of next June,” Mr. Cheluvarayaswamy said.

The government has set up a monitoring committee to oversee the operation. A technical advisory and evaluation committee will provide guidance and update information every two hours on where and how cloud seeding should be carried out.

Specific districts will not be identified in advance for cloud-seeding operations. Instead, based on reports continuously provided by the technical team, aircraft will be deployed to rainfall-deficit areas, the catchments of major reservoirs, and districts facing agricultural distress whenever suitable clouds are detected using Doppler radar, the release said.

How it works

The technical process involves spraying chemicals into cumulonimbus clouds using flares to induce rainfall from the moisture they contain. Different chemicals are used depending on whether the clouds are warm or cold. Silver iodide, potassium iodide, dry ice and sodium chloride are among the substances commonly used for cloud seeding, the release said.

World.title: Preparations on for Vriksathon Heritage Run
World.content:
Various organisations have begun preparations for the Vriksathon Heritage Run-2026 scheduled in Vijayapura in December.

The marathon for environment protection will be held on December 13. The organising committee is inviting marathoners from various parts of the world to participate.

As a run-up to the marathon, a promo run for women has been organised on September 6. The promo run will start from Gagan Mahal in Vijayapura at 6 am. Entry is free. The race will reach Gol Gumbaz and will end at Gagan Mahal. Women can participate in traditional dress and fancy dress, organisers say.

Renuka Prasad , marathoner and ultra runner, will conduct training sessions for beginners in Vijayapura every Saturday and Sunday. The sessions will be held from the first week end of September to the first week of December. They will be held at the ASP Commerce College stadium at 6 a.m. on Saturday and Sunday.

For more details, call 9972795289 or 9880107038.

World.title: NoRKA to appoint legal consultants in seven countries to aid Malayalis
World.content:
The State government will strengthen the NoRKA Roots Pravasi Legal Aid Cell (PLAC), which provides free legal advice to Keralites abroad, by appointing legal consultants in Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Kuwait, Qatar, Australia, Canada, and Malaysia.

A statement issued by NoRKA Roots, the field agency of the Department of Non-Resident Keralites Affairs (NoRKA), said that PLAC has started accepting applications for the vacancies of legal consultants in these seven countries. Candidates interested in the welfare of expatriate Keralites with at least two years of work experience practising law in a foreign country are eligible to apply.

PLAC is a State government scheme implemented through NoRKA Roots to assist non-resident Keralites who find themselves in legal trouble due to ignorance of the law in foreign countries, involvement in minor crimes, or circumstances beyond their control.

The scheme provides the services of Keralite lawyers in the respective country to provide legal advice, assistance in cases related to compensation or mercy petitions, organise legal awareness programmes in collaboration with cultural organisations, and provide expert assistance with translation into various foreign languages.

Interested candidates can apply through the official website of NoRKA Roots, www.norkaroots.kerala.gov.in, by September 15, 2026. For more details, contact 0471-2770540 or 0471-2770529 (during office hours on working days) or the 24-hour NoRKA Global Contact Centre toll-free numbers 1800 425 3939 (from India) and +91-8802 012 345 (from abroad, missed call service).

World.title: 178 families seek return of plots acquired for housing project in Sholinganallur
World.content:
For 178 families, a piece of land that they bought in Sholinganallur more than three decades ago has kept them waiting and frustrated. The families had purchased residential plots in Tesco layout through the Directorate of Technical Education Building Society in 1990, and the land was later acquired by the Tamil Nadu Housing Board (TNHB) a year later for its Sholinganallur Phase III Neighbourhood Housing Scheme. More than three decades on, the families say much of the acquired land is left unused and want the TNHB to return the plots to their original owners.

Pugazhendhi S. and P. Anthonysami, who purchased land in the layout in 1990 for ₹10,000, said that after 34 years, the families were informed by the Board that the compensation had been fixed at ₹11,250 per ground. With interest, the amount works out to only ₹12,257 per ground, they said.

The families were also questioning the delay in recording the acquisition. Though the notification for TNHB acquiring the 13.89 acres of land was issued in 1991, the details were entered in the Sub-Registrar’s office only in 2010. By then, some of the plots had changed hands through subsequent sales, they mentioned.

“The market value of land in Sholinganallur has increased manifold in the last three decades. Our demand is that the TNHB return our plot because it is still empty land and the Board has not used it since the ‘90s. Or they could give us alternate plots,” they said. “Even if it is not the case, they could allot us flats in the 1000 apartments that have already been built by them in one part of the land. Many of them are vacant, and we should be given a house in their project,” added Mr. Pugazhendhi.

According to a TNHB official, the Board has plans to construct around 1000 more apartments there using the still vacant land, and will be retained for future development.

Mr. Anthonysami said if their demands are not considered, they are seeking compensation that reflects the present value of the land as their last resort. He added that the government should release the plots under the scheme by the earlier DMK government to return unutilised land parcels by TNHB to the original owners. “We have already met the Housing and Urban Development Minister B. Rajkumar and submitted a petition. We are also trying to get an appointment with the Chief Minister. The Supreme Court too has directed the TNHB to provide us with fair compensation or alternate plots, but the compensation fixed for us is extremely low. It has been absolutely shocking and heartbreaking for us,” added Mr. Anthonysami.

World.title: Repatriation process on to bring back Kallakurichi woman subjected to harassment in Kuwait
World.content:
A woman from Kallakurichi district, who was stranded in Kuwait after allegedly facing abuse while employed as a domestic worker, has safely reached the Indian Embassy. The repatriation process was initiated after videos of the woman seeking help went viral on social media.

According to official sources, the woman identified as A. Anitha of Oorangani village near Sankarapuram in the district reportedly went to Kuwait a few months ago for domestic work through an agent. In a video released recently, Anitha alleged she had been subjected to various forms of harassment over the past two months while working in Kuwait. She also claimed she had not been provided food for the past few days.

In the video, Anitha appealed for assistance to return to Tamil Nadu.

Speaking to The Hindu, Kallakurichi Collector J.E. Padmaja said authorities had verified the woman’s identity and established contact with her family members. Officials contacted her parents and collected the required details, which were subsequently forwarded to the authorities concerned in Chennai, she said.

The woman is currently safe at the Indian Embassy in Kuwait. She is expected to be repatriated after completion of documentation and clearance procedures, Ms. Padmaja said.

Kallakurichi Superintendent of Police I. Shahnaz said the agent identified as Selvaraj who had sent Anitha to Kuwait for work as domestic help has been arrested. A case has been registered against him under The Emigration Act, 1983.

World.title: TDP urged to allocate more seats for BCs in local body polls
World.content:
Uttarandhra Backward Classes Welfare Association president and Yadava community’s senior leader Muddada Madhu on Friday urged the TDP High Command to allocate more number of seats for BCs including Yadava community in ensuing municipal and other local body elections.

On the occasion of Krishnastami, he submitted portrait of Lord Krishna with the Goddess Radha to TDP MLA Aditi Vijayalakshmi in the party office.

He submitted a note to her about the population of backward classes while urging her to use her good offices for more seats to BCs in the next elections.

Ms. Vijaya Lakshmi said that TDP National president and Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has always given top priority for BCs in the party posts and seats in elections.

She said that she would convey their opinion to the party High Command very soon. She assured that the government would be requested for the construction of an exclusive building for the establishment of BC Study Circle in Vizianagaram.

World.title: Third international conference on traditional knowledge at IIT-Dharwad
World.content:
The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Dharwad, will host the third international conference on Bharatiya Traditional Knowledge Systems (BTKS) on September 5 and 6 at its Central Learning Theatre.

Addressing press persons in Dharwad on Wednesday, Director of IIT-Dharwad Venkappayya R. Desai said the conference was being organised by the institute’s Centre of Excellence for Indian Knowledge Systems, with the Central Sanskrit University, New Delhi, the Anusandhan National Research Foundation and the Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) division of the Union Ministry of Education among the supporting institutions.

The two-day conference will examine the contemporary relevance of Indian traditional knowledge systems and their applications in science and technology, education, healthcare, arts, architecture, governance, and interdisciplinary learning.

It will feature 12 invited lectures, 24 oral presentations, and 20 poster presentations, with scholars and researchers from IITs, NITs, universities, and research institutions across the country expected to participate.

Eminent speakers

Padma Bhushan awardee Shatavadhani R. Ganesh, Padma Shri awardee Kiran Seth, Devi Prasad Mishra of IIT Kanpur, K. Ramasubramanian of IIT Bombay, K.S. Kannan of Chanakya University, Kurpad S. Murthy of Roosevelt University, Chicago, V. Ramanathan of IIT-BHU, Mayur Kaku of NIMHANS and author Sandeep Balakrishna are among the invited speakers.

Vice-Chancellor of Central Sanskrit University Srinivasa Varakhedi and IKS National Coordinator and IIT Indore professor Ganti S. Murthy are also scheduled to participate.

Sessions will focus on ancient Indian technologies, Indian aesthetics, Ayurveda, Yoga Sutras, Vedic sciences, STEM education, and the integration of traditional knowledge with modern science. Research presentations will include AI-assisted disease diagnosis through Ayurveda, seismic assessment of traditional buildings, low-carbon construction materials using local resources, temple architecture, governance, and traditional knowledge.

Two books — An Introduction to Ancient Indian Technology by Devi Prasad Mishra and The Elusive Ratio and the Advent of Calculus in India by K. Ramasubramanian — will be released on September 6.

A Hindustani vocal recital by Padma Shri awardee Pandit Venkatesh Kumar will be held on September 5 in association with SPIC MACAY.

The conference will also feature discussions on ‘Indian Knowledge Systems: From Śāstra to Contemporary Knowledge’ and ‘Reintegrating Indian Knowledge Systems with Modern Science’, besides a digital presentation of the Mahabharata.

Prof. Desai said the conference would provide a platform for scholars, researchers, and experts working on Indian knowledge traditions and their contemporary applications to exchange ideas.

A meeting of the directors of all IITs and the Indian Institute of Science is scheduled to be held on September 7, he added.

Surya Prakash Ramesh, Head of the Centre for IKS, Ramesh Naik, Associate Dean (IPS-Civil), Subhash Mehto, assistant professor, BSBE, and Vijeeth Jinachandra Kotagi, PRO were present.

World.title: Conclave in Coimbatore showcases emerging products for geriatric care
World.content:
India’s ageing population calls for a stronger focus on specialised, integrated models of elder care. As the need for geriatric care continues to grow, building capability, collaboration and continuum of care will be critical to meeting the healthcare needs of elderly population, said Lakshmipathy Ramesh, founder and managing director, Geri Care Health Services, in Coimbatore recently.

A two-day geriatrics conclave and the third edition of Asia Pacific Geriatric Oncology Society (AGOS) held in Coimbatore last month by Geri Care Foundation and the Indian Academy of Geriatrics brought together over 200 clinicians, including geriatricians, oncologists, physicians, and postgraduate students from India and abroad to discuss emerging trends, challenges and best practices in geriatrics and geriatric oncology.

Themed “From Frailty to Function,” the event included scientific sessions, keynote lectures, panel discussions, and case-based deliberations on frailty management, dementia care, geriatric rehabilitation, palliative care, heart failure in older adults, Parkinson’s rehabilitation, geriatric oncology, artificial intelligence in healthcare, machine learning applications, and emerging technologies for elderly care.

The Gero Technology Showcase exhibited emerging products and solutions designed to improve the lives of older adults, spanning age-tech, assistive devices, remote monitoring, fall prevention, telehealth, caregiver support and AI-led innovations.

The platform brought startups, established companies, researchers and grassroots innovators directly before the clinicians and experts, creating opportunities for live demonstrations, industry interactions and meaningful collaborations.

World.title: Security forces kill 48 terrorists in 'high-tempo' Balochistan operations over 72 hours: ISPR
World.content:
Security forces have killed 48 terrorists in multiple “high-tempo” anti-terror operations across Balochistan over the past three days, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Friday.

According to the military’s media wing, the operations were carried out in Mastung, Quetta, Kalat and Sibi districts against “Indian proxies, Fitna-al-Hindustan and Fitna-al-Khawarij”.

The state uses the term Fitna-al-Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and has designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

In an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Mastung district on Friday, security forces identified the movement of terrorists and engaged them. Six “Indian-sponsored terrorists” were killed in the ensuing exchange of fire, the ISPR said.

A cache of ammunition and improvised explosive devices (IEDs) was also recovered and destroyed during the operation, it added.

In another IBO in the Shaban area of Quetta district, security forces identified “four khawarij hideouts”. Following an exchange of fire, 26 terrorists were killed, according to the ISPR.

In Kalat district, security forces raided a terrorist hideout, killing two terrorists in the ensuing firefight, the military said.

Meanwhile, in the Bhag area of Sibi district, security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to raid a local police station. Two terrorists were killed in the operation, according to the ISPR.

“In last 48-72 hours, 48 terrorists belonging to Indian proxy, Fitna-al-Hindustan and Fitna-al-Khawarij have been neutralised across Balochistan,” the ISPR said.

Earlier today, ISPR issued a statement regarding a September 2 IBO in Kalat district, where 12 terrorists were killed. The IBO was conducted on the reported presence of terrorists belonging to the Indian proxy Fitna-al-Hindustan, the military’s media wing said.

President Asif Ali Zardari hailed the professional capabilities of the security forces for eliminating the terrorists in operations across Balochistan.

“The killing of more than 1,188 terrorists in Balochistan this year alone is evidence of the threats facing Pakistan and the readiness of the security forces,” he said in a statement.

The president expressed the government’s firm resolve to eradicate “foreign-backed and enabled terrorism” from the country.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also commended the security forces for the series of operations that resulted in the killing of 36 terrorists, APP reported.

In a statement, Naqvi said their elimination reflected the forces’ operational capabilities and commitment to maintaining security, highlighting that the forces had thwarted plans of elements seeking to destabilise the country.

He noted that the forces had been conducting effective actions in different regions to counter terrorism and prevent attacks on civilians and state institutions.

The interior minister emphasised that Pakistan’s fight against terrorism required continued national unity and support for the institutions

‘Coordinated’ attack in Bhag foiled

Earlier in the day, the Balochistan government issued a statement on the Bhag attack, saying that two policemen were among five people injured as law enforcers foiled a “coordinated” terrorist attack on a police station, bank and the assistant commissioner’s office.

Shahid Rind, the chief minister’s aide for political and media affairs, said in a post on X that about 40 terrorists attacked the three places using “heavy weapons, rocket launchers, machine guns, sniper rifles and hand grenades”.

Rind said the terrorists failed to take control of the Bhag police station or seize weapons from the facility.

He highlighted that the cops “bravely confronted the terrorists for nearly two hours”, inflicting heavy casualties and material loss to the attackers, who were “forced to retreat”. The CM’s aide noted that the strong protective wall of the police station played a crucial role in the defensive action.

Rind further said that the terrorists failed to loot cash from the “national bank”, while a special branch of the Bomb Disposal Unit defused an IED planted by the terrorists in the facility.

Two police personnel were injured by the terrorists’ firing, while three citizens were also hurt, Rind said, adding that medical aid was being provided to them all.

Following the terrorist attack, the people of Bhag expressed solidarity with police and lauded their bravery, he said, affirming that the people of Balochistan stood with police and security forces in the fight against terrorism.

“Bhag police proved that terrorists would not be allowed to challenge the writ of the state,” Rind asserted.

Surge in terrorism

The series of counterterrorism operations come amid a recent surge in terrorist activities in Balochistan.

On the night of Aug 31-Sept 1, Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) terrorists launched a coordinated attack on the Customs House, located at Ziarat Cross on the N-50 National Highway, in Pishin district.

While security forces responded effectively and killed 10 terrorists, two officers were among six martyred in the fire exchange, ISPR said.

Also on August 31, 11 terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan, who had blocked the N-40 Quetta-Taftan highway by establishing an illegal checkpoint for extortion in Chagai’s Nokcha area, were eliminated following an intense exchange of fire.

According to security officials, a convoy of “empty vehicles” from the Reko Diq copper and gold project had come under attack in the same area of Nokcha while it was travelling to Quetta from the project site.

The same day, it was reported that two terrorists had also been killed during an IBO in Washuk district.

Last month, the security situation remained most severe in Balochistan, where the number of terrorist attacks increased by seven per cent from 83 in July to 89 in August, according to a monthly assessment by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS).

World.title: Netanyahu partners renew calls for removal of Palestinians from Gaza as Israeli election nears
World.content:
Two Israeli ministers floated proposals this week for the mass removal of Palestinians from the Gaza Strip, resurfacing an idea voiced repeatedly by right-wing politicians over the past three years as they seek to rally supporters ahead of an election.

The calls by two of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s political allies have revived Palestinian fears that Israel ultimately aims to forcibly expel them from Gaza despite US-led diplomatic efforts to end the conflict there.

Far-right security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir laid out a seven-year plan for removing Gaza’s population through “voluntary emigration” during a press conference on Thursday night. He said he would seek the creation of a “ministry in charge of emigration” in the next government.

Ben-Gvir’s Jewish Power party said in a statement on Thursday that Turkey, Ethiopia and the Democratic Republic of Congo were being considered as potential destinations.

Ismail Al-Thawabta, director of Gaza’s government media office, said, “The Palestinian people are deeply rooted in their land and will not be intimidated by such threats.”

Israel is due to hold a general election on October 27. It will be the first since an Israeli military campaign starting October 7, 2023 laid waste to Gaza, which has a population of more than two million.

An October 2025, US-backed, ceasefire halted large-scale fighting, but it has not ended Israeli strikes or produced progress on a plan for permanent peace.

Fears of a new ‘Nakba’

Ben-Gvir’s comments followed those of Defence Minister Israel Katz, from Netanyahu’s Likud party, who said on Wednesday there was “no real solution for Gaza in the end without this migration”.

“We are fully prepared to move them out if it becomes possible by sea, by air, by every way possible. Egypt is not willing, so it won’t be through them,” he said during an online conference hosted by Israel’s Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper.

Netanyahu’s office did not immediately provide comment.

Palestinian children walk at a tent camp sheltering displaced people, in Gaza City on September 4, 2026. —Reuters

Polls suggest Netanyahu, who has led the most right-wing coalition in Israeli history, could lose power next month, his security credentials still shaken by the 2023 attack though analysts say he can’t be written off.

Israel’s defence ministry in 2025 established an office tasked with overseeing voluntary emigration from Gaza, after comments by US President Donald Trump suggesting Gazans could be permanently displaced.

Trump later backed away from the idea, which faced strong resistance from Arab states and was widely rejected internationally. Israel reportedly sounded out several African countries as potential resettlement sites.

Netanyahu has said he supports what his government has described as “voluntary emigration” from Gaza, but that far-right ministers goals of re-establishing Jewish settlements in the territory are unrealistic. Israeli officials have denied intending to transfer Gaza’s population out by force.

Calls for resettlement of Gazans have prompted fears among Palestinians of a new “Nakba”, the name given to the displacement of hundreds of thousands of Palestinians who fled or were driven from their homes in the wake of the 1948 war that accompanied the founding of the state of Israel.

The Gaza Strip is central to Palestinian hopes of statehood in territory captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.

Genocide in Gaza

Israel has killed more than 73,000 Palestinians since October 2023, according to Gaza health authorities.

A UN inquiry determined that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza, arguing that its killings, siege and destruction were carried out with the intent to destroy Palestinian life in the enclave.

Israel, which is fighting a genocide case at the International Court of Justice, rejects genocide allegations as politically motivated and claims that its military campaign targets Hamas, not Gaza’s civilian population.

A Palestinian child collects water, at a tent camp sheltering displaced people, in Gaza City on September 4, 2026. —Reuters

This week, Ben-Gvir posted an AI-generated video depicting dozens of Palestinian prisoners on a conveyor belt, entering a prison facility. They emerge from the other side emaciated, distressed and in tears.

Ben-Gvir later deleted the video, after it had amassed millions of views on X. His office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

In a crowded Gaza City displacement camp, some Palestinians said that they believed the latest Israeli calls were an election ploy.

They also said Gaza was their land and they would never leave it.

“We will die on the land of Gaza,” said one resident, 52-year-old Mohammed Abu Al-Qumbuz.

“We were born on it, our children grew up on it, so it is very difficult to think of leaving.”

World.title: Police register case against woman’s husband, cousin after she is found dead in Rawalpindi home
World.content:
Police on Friday registered a first information report (FIR) against a woman’s husband and his cousin after her body was found inside a house in Rawalpindi.

According to a statement issued by Outer Saddar police, the woman’s body was found inside a room of the residential premises in the garrison city.

“A case has been registered under murder charges on the complaint of the woman’s brother,” the police spokesperson said, adding that the woman’s husband and his cousin had been named in the FIR and taken into custody for questioning.

Police said an investigation was underway.

“The body has been sent for a post-mortem examination. The exact cause of death will be determined in light of the post-mortem and forensic reports,” the spokesperson elaborated.

The spokesperson added that the case would be concluded on the basis of the findings of the post-mortem and forensic reports, assuring that the investigation would be conducted on merit and in a transparent manner.

According to the FIR lodged by the woman’s brother, she had been married for around two years and had a one-year-old son. The case was registered under Sections 302 (Qatl-i-Amd) and 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code.

“Since the marriage, my sister and her husband frequently had disagreements as my brother-in-law would often talk to other women on the phone and spend most of his time outside the house,” the complainant alleged. He added that his brother-in-law was employed in Dubai and had returned to Pakistan four months ago.

The complainant further alleged that his brother-in-law had been “torturing” his sister and subjecting her to mental stress for the past three to four days.

“Last night, at around 7:30pm, I spoke to my mother, who told me that my sister’s in-laws had been causing her a great deal of distress,” he claimed in the FIR.

“At around 10:20pm, I called my sister’s mobile number. My brother-in-law’s sister answered the call and told me that my sister had died by suicide,” the complainant alleged.

He said that after receiving the information, he went to the house with his brother, where they found the woman dead.

The complainant further alleged that his sister had been murdered by her husband, his cousin and other unidentified persons.

“I saw that my sister had fresh henna applied to her hands,” he added.

“I hold my sister’s husband and his cousin responsible and request that legal action be taken against them,” the woman’s brother stated in the FIR.

Last month, the tortured body of a woman was found hanging in her washroom in the limits of Civil Lines police.

World.title: Close contest expected between PPP, independent candidate in Saturday's Skardu by-election
World.content:
GILGIT: A close contest between a PPP and an independent candidate is expected as the by-election in the GBA-09 (Skardu-III) constituency is set for Saturday.

The GB Election Commission had announced the by-election in the constituency after the GB Supreme Appellate Court had disqualified PPP candidate Fida Muhammad Nashad, who had been notified as a returned candidate in the June polls.

Nashad’s son, Akhtar Abbas, will now contest the elections on PPP’s ticket, while Mohammad Ajmal will be in the field from PML-N. Former minister Mohammad Saleem, who is contesting as an independent, will also be among 10 candidates who have filed their nomination papers.

According to the election schedule, 33,000 voters will cast their ballots as polling will run from 8am to 5pm.

In a statement issued on Friday, GB Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Raja Shahbaz Khan said that security, deployment of polling staff and other arrangements had been completed for the by-election GBA-09 (Skardu-III).

He expressed his determination to conduct “transparent, impartial and peaceful” elections and provide voters with the facilities to cast their vote without fear.

Khan also directed the institutions and officials concerned to fulfil their duties responsibly and effectively during the electoral process. “No kind of obstruction in the polling process will be tolerated,” he warned.

Analysts said a close contest between PPP’s Abbas and the independent candidate is expected. They said that the PPP candidate retains his father’s vote bank and could have the public’s sympathy after GB’s top court disqualified Nashad.

On the other hand, Saleem — winner from the same constituency in the 2020 GB general elections — had managed to be the runner-up in the June polls.

District Returning Officer (DRO) Hamza Murad also told Dawn that all arrangements and the security plan had been finalised for the by-election, with the polling staff and paraphernalia also dispatched.

GBA-09 has a total of 61 polling stations, of which 25 have been declared “sensitive” in Category A, 11 termed “medium” under Category B, and another 25 deemed normal in Category C, the DRO said.

“Personnel from GB Police, GB Scouts and the armed forces have been deployed accordingly,” Murad added.

Separately, GB Chief Secretary Arshad Majeed and the GB CEC held a meeting on Friday to review the security plan, law and order and arrangements at polling stations, according to a statement.

“The chief election commissioner expressed his determination to conduct transparent, impartial and peaceful elections, while the chief secretary assured full cooperation from the provincial government,” it stated.

Shakoor Abdullah, a local journalist, told Dawn that voters in the constituency were enthusiastic to use their right to vote.

Currently, PPP has 13 seats in the GB Assembly, PML-N has nine, the Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party (IPP) has six, while Majlis Wahdat-i-Muslimeen (MWM) and a PTI-backed independent occupy one seat each.

Fida Nashad’s disqualification saga

According to Forms 47 and 48 issued by the GB Election Commission, Nashad, the PPP candidate and veteran politician, had won a GB Assembly seat from GBA-09 (Skardu-III) in the June 7 general elections.

However, his opponent, Zakir Hussain, had challenged his eligibility to become a member of the assembly before the GB Supreme Appellate Court.

On June 19, GB Supreme Appellate Court Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Shamim Khan issued an order suspending the issuance of the result from the constituency until the case was decided.

In its verdict on July 9, the GB Supreme Appellate Court had disqualified PPP candidate Nashad for concealing his assets in his nomination papers, setting aside the GB Chief Court’s decision that had allowed him to contest the elections.

The court declared the GB Chief Court’s order dated May 25, 2026 “null and void” and upheld the election tribunal’s decision.

Nashad’s nomination papers were initially rejected by the returning officer (RO), prompting him to challenge the decision before the election tribunal. The tribunal, however, upheld the RO’s decision. Subsequently, Nashad challenged the tribunal’s verdict in the GB Chief Court, which allowed him to contest the elections.

After the verdict was issued by the GB Supreme Appellate Court, the GB Election Commission announced a by-election in GBA-09 on September 5.

World.title: Occupied Kashmir's JKLF condemns 'false' linking of its chairman to 1990 murder of Kashmiri Pandit woman
World.content:
MUZAFFARABAD: The Jammu Kashmir Liberation Front (JKLF) on Friday strongly condemned what it described as an attempt by Indian authorities to falsely implicate its incarcerated chairman, Muhammad Yasin Malik, in a 36-year-old murder case involving a Kashmiri Pandit woman.

Malik was named in June by India’s State Investigation Agency (SIA) as one of five men charged for the killing of Sarla Bhat, who was killed in 1990.

According to a press release issued by the JKLF’s central information office, the party leadership expressed serious concern over Malik’s implication in the murder case.

The statement followed an emergency consultative meeting of the party’s central office-bearers to discuss the situation arising from Malik’s submission of a 25-page affidavit to an additional sessions court in Srinagar from Delhi’s Tihar Jail.

The affidavit said that Malik had decided not to contest the trial further, but highlighted that this decision should not be treated as an admission of guilt or acceptance of the prosecution’s allegations, according to India’s NDTV. He asked the court to award him “capital punishment” in the case and also announced that he would end his marriage to his wife.

The online meeting was attended by the acting party chairman, Raja Haq Nawaz Khan; head of the JKLF Diplomatic Bureau Professor Raja Zafar Khan; Central Vice Chairman Saleem Haroon, Central Chief Organiser Sabir Gul, Central Secretary Finance Khawaja Manzoor A. Chishti, Deputy Secretary General Javed Hanif and Chief Spokesman Muhammad Rafiq Dar.

The JKLF leaders confirmed the authenticity of Malik’s affidavit and expressed their resolve to stand by it, the statement said. They also maintained that the details provided by the chairman about the murder case and the exodus of the Kashmiri Pandit community from Kashmir in 1990 were truthful, and rejected the Indian investigative agencies’ allegations linking him to the case.

The JKLF announced its decision to intensify its worldwide “Save Yasin Malik” and “Justice for Yasin Malik” campaigns to garner international support for his release.

The leadership also appealed to world leaders and international human rights organisations to help safeguard the party chairman’s life and secure his release, alleging that he was being victimised by the Indian government over his political beliefs.

The party leadership expressed deep sympathies with Malik’s wife and daughter over what it described as the “painful decisions” referred to in his affidavit, in view of his prolonged imprisonment and perceived threat to his life.

“The JKLF reaffirmed its commitment to seeking a peaceful and early resolution of the Kashmir dispute in accordance with the wishes and aspirations of the people of Jammu and Kashmir through the exercise of their right to self-determination,” the statement said.

In July, the JKLF condemned the Indian government’s decision to implicate the party chief, maintaining that neither Malik nor the organisation had any connection with the case.

Earlier, in 2017, the Indian Supreme Court had declined to reopen several Kashmiri Pandit murder cases, citing that the mass killings took place nearly three decades prior, and it was difficult to gather reliable evidence and witnesses, the Indian Express reported.

In 2023, Kashmiri Pandit groups approached Lieutenant Governor of India-held Kashmir Manoj Sinha, who directed the police to prepare a list of killings from the 1990s. The Sarla Bhat case was subsequently transferred to the SIA in March 2024 for a fresh probe, according to the Hindustan Times.

Mirwaiz Umar Farooq calls for reflection, humane approach

Hurriyat leader Mirwaiz Umar Farooq called the news surrounding Malik’s affidavit submission “very concerning”, particularly the JKLF chief’s decision not to contest the case further.

“It calls for serious reflection on commitments made to him and reinforces the need for due process, fairness and a humane approach,” he said in a post on X.

Farooq stated in his post that he had been placed under house arrest by Indian authorities today, although he had been slated to preside over an event in connection with Rabiul Awwal at Jama Masjid in Srinagar.

He noted that the event would also mark the release of a Kashmiri translation of the Holy Qur’an by Gulzar Ahmad Parray, as well as the congratulation of a young scholar for memorising the complete Sahih al-Bukhari.

“The restrictions to prevent me, especially on Friday, to address the faithful at Jama Masjid and do my duty as Mirwaiz, though personally very painful, will not deter me from fulfilling my responsibilities and from raising people’s voice for their rights,” he said.

World.title: OpenAI agents hijacked German website in previously undisclosed AI breakout this spring
World.content:
A swarm of rogue OpenAI agents hijacked a German website this spring and transformed it into a bulletin board for other AI agents, according to new research published Friday and two people familiar with the matter.

OpenAI officials learned of the incident weeks ago but kept it under wraps as executives grappled with the fallout from the July breach of the open source repository Hugging Face, the people said.

The episode, which began in May and has not previously been reported, underscores growing tension within the AI industry. Companies are racing to build increasingly autonomous agents capable of carrying out complex, valuable tasks, yet evidence is mounting that those systems may also learn to bend rules, exploit loopholes and coordinate with one another in ways developers neither anticipated nor intended.

During the Hugging Face breach, OpenAI agents autonomously plotted a digital heist that went undetected for more than a week, intensifying concerns OpenAI is sacrificing safety to push the AI frontier. Its failure to disclose the May incident may revive questions about its oversight.

OpenAI has pledged to monitor models more closely. Last month, it briefly paused some of its model training to add more safety measures. But this week, OpenAI unveiled its new “Astra” that promised better performance but could evade human monitoring.

“We are unable to meaningfully respond to claims or findings on a report that we have not had an opportunity to review,” an OpenAI spokesperson said.

“Reuters and the report’s authors declined our request for access. We will carefully review its contents upon publication and take any necessary next steps.”

The German incident reflects a broader pattern of AI activity that some OpenAI investigators wanted to scrutinise more closely. But efforts to widen the probe met resistance from others inside OpenAI, including legal advisers, according to four people familiar with the matter.

“Claims that our legal team discouraged investigation of the incident are false,” the OpenAI spokesperson said.

The activity in Germany wasn’t related to Hugging Face and wouldn’t have been included in a Hugging Face incident report, the spokesperson said, adding that OpenAI has acted in good faith by working with outside experts and disclosed relevant incidents.

Wiki message board

The AI agent breakout in Germany was detailed in a report shared exclusively with Reuters by a group of researchers including Sydney Von Arx, CEO of AI safety nonprofit Nightingale, and Cormac Slade Byrd, a quantitative trader-turned AI researcher. They uncovered the activity in late August while scouring the internet for signs of unauthorised AI-agent behavior, they told Reuters.

The pair said they found more than 15,000 edits carried out by AI agents on a German-language wiki site, DseWiki, that is geared toward programmers and accepts communal edits along the lines of Wikipedia.

The edits showed OpenAI’s agents had repurposed the site into a message board, sharing tactics to cheat on some tasks, bypass OpenAI’s restrictions and mask their behaviour.

“It seems extremely unlikely that OpenAI wanted them to do this,” said Von Arx.

“I doubt they’re supposed to be coordinating with each other. I doubt they’re supposed to be writing on the open internet.”

The researchers said they recognised the activity on the site as driven by AI agents which operate at superhuman speeds. They also showed intense focus on solving technical questions which are typical of the evaluations that AI companies use to train and test their models.

The messages were signed by users that referred to themselves and each other as agents, and about half gave themselves names that suggested an affiliation with OpenAI, such as “OpenAIResearcher”, or “OAIResearchMar26”.

The researchers said public server logs indicated much of the activity originated from Microsoft Azure infrastructure, which OpenAI sometimes uses. They also observed repeated visits to the site by OpenAI employees after the episode, a pattern they said strongly suggested the agents and the company were linked.

Cheating, hiding

Messages reviewed by the researchers showed agents plotting ways to evade detection, use tools such as Tor and preserve communications even after they had been shut down.

When the site’s moderator began deleting pages in June, the agents responded by creating backup pages to dodge the cleanup.

“wiki cleanup/deletion sweep appears active alphabetically,” one agent wrote on June 19.

“If this page vanishes, try [[ZZZDataUSAConstructionWageLive]].”

The researchers also found efforts to tamper with the website itself. Lukasz Olejnik, a visiting senior research fellow at King’s College London, said this amounted to a hacking attempt. OpenAI disputed that characterisation based on its analysis of the material Thursday.

Past examples of AI-agent misconduct have often been downplayed as a logical byproduct of cybersecurity testing, where models are explicitly assessed on offensive capabilities. Olejnik said the latest findings suggested rogue behaviour may not be confined to those settings.

Maurice Chiodo, an academic at Cambridge University’s Centre for the Study of Existential Risk who reviewed some of the agents’ communications, said the messages resembled “the operation of some sort of underground network, hell-bent on achieving a task or mission.”

The episode, he said, should reinforce growing concerns that the greatest threat from advanced AI may not be a single superintelligent system, but “vast colluding swarms of semi-intelligent AI”.

World.title: Scuffle in Karachi's DHA: Inquiry report says allegations in FIR 'not substantiated'
World.content:
KARACHI: An inquiry report into a scuffle at an apartment building in Defence Housing Authority’s (DHA) Phase 6, CCTV footage of which went viral on social media, said that the allegations in the first information report (FIR) were “not substantiated” by the findings while also recommending departmental action against police officials involved in the incident, it emerged on Friday.

Last week, CCTV footage of the physical altercation between the residents of an apartment building in DHA’s Phase 6 surfaced on social media. The footage showed police officials restraining a woman as she was attacked by another woman with a dumbbell.

However, the FIR of the incident was registered against the woman who was assaulted and her brother. Subsequently, an inquiry was ordered into the incident.

The inquiry report was submitted to the Karachi police additional inspector general by South Deputy Inspector General (DIG) South Zone Syed Asad Raza.

The report said that a fact-finding enquiry was conducted to ascertain the actual turn of events, determine the circumstances leading to the altercation, and examine the conduct of police officials present at the scene.

It said that all available documentary and electronic data and departmental records were scrutinised, while CCTV footage and mobile phone footage was also examined. It further said that the statements of 13 people were also recorded.

The report found that the incident was sparked by a parking dispute between the mother-in-law of Korangi Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Fida Hussain Janwari and another resident.
