World.title: Chinese investors explore manufacturing, energy projects in Uzbekistan’s Fergana
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 4. Chinese companies are exploring new investment projects in Uzbekistan’s Fergana region, with potential cooperation spanning nonwoven materials, road construction and petrochemicals.

This was reflected in the statement by the Fergana regional administration, following a meeting between Fergana Region Governor Khayrullo Bozorov and representatives of Chinese companies Zhicheng Nonwovens (Jiangsu) Co., Ltd., San Zheng International and Sora Energy to discuss expanding investment cooperation and developing new projects in promising sectors.

During the meeting, the sides reviewed Zhicheng Nonwovens’ experience and capabilities in producing nonwoven materials used in medical and hygiene products. San Zheng International presented its capabilities in producing asphalt concrete mixtures and road construction materials, while Sora Energy outlined its activities in petrochemical production, including special additives designed to improve fuel quality.

The Chinese investors expressed interest in implementing several new investment projects in Fergana and presented proposals covering potential areas and prospects for cooperation.

“Fergana has all the necessary opportunities to support investors’ initiatives and provide the conditions and infrastructure required for project implementation,” the regional administration quoted Bozorov as saying.

The meeting also highlighted the growing interest of Chinese businesses in Fergana, which the regional administration attributed to expanding cooperation and an established atmosphere of mutual trust between the sides.

According to the administration, Chinese companies are already implementing a number of major investment projects in the region. The latest proposals could further diversify Chinese investment in Fergana by adding projects in industrial materials, road infrastructure and higher-value petrochemical production.

The sides agreed to continue cooperation on developing and implementing new mutually beneficial investment projects, with the regional administration expected to support investors in advancing the proposed initiatives.

World.title: At President Ilham Aliyev’s initiative, new Baku Metro station named “September 20”
World.content:
Photo: Press service of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan

BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 4. The new metro station of the Baku Metro, located at 194 Jalil Mammadguluzade Street, Nasimi District, will be named "September 20".

Prime Minister Ali Asadov signed the relevant resolution.

According to the resolution, in light of the restoration of the state sovereignty of the Republic of Azerbaijan throughout the country on September 20, 2023, and at the initiative of Ilham Aliyev, President of the Republic of Azerbaijan, the new station of the Baku Metro, located at Baku, Nasimi District, 194 Jalil Mammadguluzade Street, has been named “September 20.”

The Baku City Executive Authority and the closed joint-stock company “Baku Metro” have been instructed to resolve any issues arising from this decision.

According to a decree by President Ilham Aliyev dated September 19, 2024, September 20 is celebrated in Azerbaijan as State Sovereignty Day. This date was established to commemorate the full restoration of Azerbaijan’s sovereignty throughout the country following the local counterterrorism measures conducted on September 19–20, 2023.

World.title: Russian drone attack hits Ukraine's SBU headquarters in Kyiv
World.content:
A Russian drone hit the headquarters of Ukraine's SBU security service in Kyiv, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said, vowing to retaliate as Moscow kept up its constant air attacks on the capital for the tenth day.

Heavy black smoke rose in Kyiv city centre following the attack, on Friday, local time, which signalled a new escalation in the conflict. At least seven people were injured, Kyiv's mayor said.

Twelve killed as Russia steps up aerial assault on Ukraine Russia carries out a sixth straight day of heavy attacks on Kyiv, with civilian infrastructure and residential buildings among the targets.

During more than four-and-a-half years of war with Russia, Ukrainian government buildings have rarely been damaged in drone and missile strikes.

The SBU is vital to Ukraine's war efforts as it executes high-impact, deep strikes to damage Russia's war machine and its energy infrastructure.

"The drone was aimed directly at the office of the Head of the Security Service in that building," Mr Zelenskyy said on the Telegram app.

It was not immediately clear if SBU members were among the injured.

Ukraine vows 'tangible' response

Mr Zelenskyy said that he ordered "an appropriate, tangible response and, where possible, one that mirrors this strike, to the Russians once everything was ready".

Numerous ambulances and emergency services were heading to the scene in the historic part of the city close to the Saint Sophia Cathedral, a UNESCO World Heritage site.

The owner of a popular bakery, Zavertailo, said on the Telegram app that their building located opposite the SBU building was also destroyed in the attack.

Russian drones targeted downtown Kyiv and Ukraine's SBU headquarters, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. (AP: Francisco Seco)

One woman shouted into her phone that she had popped out to buy cigarettes and been startled by the explosion.

Ukraine's capital has been under continuous Russian drone attack for 10 days. On Wednesday, a university in the city centre was also hit.

"I think (people) can get used to this. In the centre of Kyiv, and in the centre of Moscow. It will get worse, I believe this," said Oleh, 33, who declined to give his last name.

'Rejection of diplomacy'

Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha urged allies to step up pressure on Moscow after a Russian drone hit Ukraine's security service headquarters in central Kyiv.

"The Russian attack on Ukraine’s Security Service Headquarters is a major escalation that demands resolute responses," he said on X.

"Moscow launched this strike during a renewed push for peace - laying bare its true rejection of diplomacy," he said.

The SBU is a vast and secretive agency responsible for ambitious operations against Russia, such as the 2022 bombing of a Russian bridge to occupied Crimea and a 2025 drone attack, codenamed Spiderweb, that struck Russian strategic bombers.

It is also widely seen as a leading player in a campaign of covert assassinations of senior Russian military and other figures blamed by Ukraine for carrying out war crimes. Russia has denounced those killings as terrorist attacks.

Reuters

World.title: Argentina's Milei vows Falklands oil sanctions in sovereignty push
World.content:
Argentine President Javier Milei says he will sanction oil companies drilling in the Falkland Islands, the British overseas territory claimed by Argentina.

Mr Milei's comments come days after US President Donald Trump said he was reviewing the United States' neutral position on the remote archipelago in the South Atlantic.

It is 44 years since Argentina was defeated by Britain in a war over the islands that killed hundreds, but its sovereignty claim is still enshrined in the constitution and frequently invoked as an expression of national identity.

Now years after a deadly war and unresolved sovereignty claims, tensions are once again escalating.

Javier Milei delivers TV address

Argentina's President Javier Milei delivered a national address on Thursday, local time, and said the "winds of change" favoured his country's claim to the archipelago, known in Argentina as the Malvinas.

UK urges action over Falklands banner The British government urges FIFA to investigate after Argentine players held up a banner declaring the Falkland Islands were Argentinian.

He then announced sweeping actions aimed at stopping the development of the deep-sea Sea Lion oil project about 220 kilometres north of the islands.

British company Rockhopper Exploration and Israel's Navitas Petroleum plan to begin drilling in the coming months and start pumping oil in 2028. Argentina considers the project an illegal exploitation of resources in waters it claims as its own.

The companies said in a statement: "The partnership believes that the recent developments are not expected to have a material effect on the development activities of the Sea Lion Project, including the timetable for completion of the Project's development."

The Argentine leader threatened tougher sanctions against companies involved in the offshore drilling.

He also announced new funding for a naval base in Argentina's southernmost province of Tierra del Fuego to bolster the country's military presence near the islands.

"Argentina will not stand idly by," Mr Milei said.

" Any further advance on the Malvinas Islands will be considered a violation of our national security. "

Donald Trump reviewing US position

Argentina maintains that it inherited sovereignty over the islands from its former coloniser, Spain, and that Britain has illegally occupied them since 1833.

Britain rejects that claim, citing the islanders' desire to remain a British overseas territory.

For decades, successive US administrations have remained neutral on the competing claims while recognising Britain's de facto administration of the islands.

On Monday, Donald Trump stirred concern in Britain when asked whether his administration was reviewing its stance on the decades-old dispute.

"I always review every position," he replied.

"That's just one of many."

Donald Trumps has put UK support in doubt. (Reuters: Evelyn Hockstein)

Then, in an interview aired Thursday with British broadcaster GB News, Mr Trump dodged directly answering a question about whether the US would "come to the aid" of Britain in another conflict over the Falklands.

Instead, he repeated past complaints that Britain had not provided sufficient support for the US-led bombing campaign against Iran.

"Your country was not there to help me," Mr Trump said, recalling Britain's former prime minister, Keir Starmer, telling him the country did not have ships to contribute to the campaign.

"It was pretty sad, the whole thing."

Mr Milei presented Washington's review of its stance as a vindication of his policies and full-throated support for the Trump administration.

"The United States is considering this change of position because it knows that Argentina has a reliable partner," he said.

Britain, by contrast, is "on a path of decline", he said, alleging it faced "multiple migratory, demographic, and economic crises".

British commitment 'unshakeable'

Britain, which has controlled the islands since 1833, has said that Falkland islanders should determine their own future.

British defence secretary Wes Streeting said on Friday, local time, that the people living there had chosen to be British.

"Milei's statement overnight tells us more about domestic politics in Argentina than it does about the Falkland Islands," Mr Streeting said on X.

"Our commitment to the Falklands is absolute and unshakeable."

British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband also said on X, the UK's position on the Falkland Islands is unwavering.

"The Islands are British and will remain so because that is the overwhelming position of the Islanders," he said.

"Their right of self-determination is paramount, grounded in international law and we will resolutely uphold it."

In a 2013 referendum, 99.8 per cent of voters backed remaining under British rule, on a turnout of about 92 per cent. Britain cites the vote as evidence of the islanders' wishes and says it will not discuss sovereignty without their consent.

Argentina rejected the referendum.

ABC/Wires

World.title: Man jailed for recruiting underage girls for sex
World.content:
A North Queensland man motivated by his own "selfish and sinister desires" has been sentenced to 12 years' jail for the rape, sexual assault and recruitment of underage girls for sex.

Warning: This story contains details of sexual assault that some readers may find disturbing.

Charles William Gary Ottaviano previously pleaded guilty to five counts of rape, six counts of indecent treatment of a child under 16 and one count each of repeated sexual conduct with a child and sexual assault over a seven-year period.

During sentencing on Friday afternoon, the Townsville District Court heard that Ottaviano was found to have raped a child and bribed her to recruit other girls for himself and other adult men to abuse.

Four of the five complainants were under the age of 16, with the youngest aged 13 when the offences occurred.

'Your actions are appalling'

In sentencing, Judge Nathan Jarro said Ottaviano's offending was "motivated by your own selfish and sinister desires".

Four of the five complainants were under the age of 16. (ABC North Queensland: Rachael Merritt)

He said the "predatory" behaviour showed "features of manipulation and corruption … money, cigarettes, alcohol, secrecy and recruitment".

The court heard the 39-year-old supplied the girls with cash, alcohol, drugs and cigarettes in exchange for forcing them into sexual acts, committing "routine, repeated sexual conduct".

Judge Jarro said Ottaviano targeted and manipulated "vulnerable" children, exploiting their youth, while ignoring their "obvious pain and distress", and pleas to stop.

The court heard Ottaviano threatened one girl that she would be "bashed" if she told anyone, and laughed at another who struggled to breathe as he abused her.

Judge Jarro told Ottaviano that a complainant who was 13 at the time of offending "never wanted to have sex with you" but she was young and scared.

'History of trauma'

When handing down the sentence, Judge Jarro said he considered Ottaviano's traumatic and "deprived" past, where drugs, sex and violence "sadly became the norm".

Judge Jarro noted Ottaviano had undergone sexual offenders' treatment in late 2024.

Ottaviano has already served two years of his 12-year sentence in pre-sentence custody.

No parole eligibility date has been set.

World.title: Romanian prosecutors indict Tate brothers for trafficking minors, laundering charges
World.content:
Romanian prosecutors has officially indicted manosphere influencer Andrew Tate for trafficking minors, among other charges, alongside his brother Tristan.

On Friday, local time, Andrew Tate was indicted on charges of trafficking minors, money laundering, sex with a minor and witness tampering.

His brother Tristan was indicted for complicity.

The Tate brothers, former kickboxers with dual US and British citizenship, were arrested in Miami in late July after Britain requested their extradition.

Mainly based in Romania since 2017, they have been under criminal investigation in the country on charges including human trafficking since December 2022.

They have denied all wrongdoing.

Geek culture' revealed as pipeline to misogyny Researchers say the manosphere has gone mainstream as young men who were suckered into the space reveal how they were recruited into the space.

Romanian prosecutors allege the Tates recruited their victims by seducing them and falsely claiming to want a relationship or marriage, before forcing them to produce pornographic content for a webcam business.

"We will examine every aspect of [the indictment] with the same level of scrutiny and we will challenge any evidential, procedural or legal deficiencies through the appropriate judicial process," a Romanian lawyer for the Tates, Eugen Vidineac, said in a statement.

"Our clients continue to reject the allegations against them."

The Tate brothers remain in jail in the US while a judge decides on the request for their extradition to Britain where they are wanted on rape charges.

Supporters of Andrew and Tristan Tate wait for the latest on their US case. (Reuters: Marco Bello)

The spokesperson for the Romanian anti-organised crime prosecuting unit DIICOT, which is investigating the Tates, said it was not immediately clear whether the unit will seek their extradition from the United States.

The Tates can be tried in absentia in Romania, but the trial will not start immediately.

Under Romanian law the indictment gets sent to a preliminary court chamber where a judge will inspect the case files to ensure legality.

While the law states that the preliminary chamber judge has 60 days to finalise the report, indictments routinely take significantly longer.

DIICOT said one of Andrew Tate's victims was 15 when he seduced her in Britain in 2012, before moving her to the Romanian capital Bucharest and using physical violence and mental intimidation to sexually exploit her by forcing her to produce pornographic content for social media sites.

His brother Tristan was an accessory, the unit said, using physical aggression to coerce the victim.

Prosecutors said the brothers kept $US 1.25 million from the video chat income generated by the victim, roughly 80 per cent of all her gains.

The brothers tried to launder the funds by buying four luxury cars, they added.

Andrew Tate, a self-described misogynist, previously said he moved to Romania because law enforcement was more lax there.

Both brothers have grown their following of mainly young men by building a lavish, hyper-macho image, and by providing tips on how to coerce women.

Reuters

World.title: Jai Arrow makes emotional 100th Souths appearance, Souths thrash Roosters
World.content:
Tears flowed as Jai Arrow made his 100th Rabbitohs appearance, with his Souths teammates helping crush the reserve team of their arch rivals, the Roosters.

Arrow choked back tears when he was hugged by Wayne Bennett as the forward was given a hero's reception at a sold out Sydney Football Stadium.

The 31-year-old father of one was diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND) this year and, until two weeks ago, was stranded on 98 NRL games for the Bunnies.

At Bennett's initiative, the NRL allowed Souths an extra interchange against the Gold Coast last week for game number 99 and again on Friday against the Roosters.

"It was pretty emotional," Cam Murray told Channel 9.

"I'm just so happy that everyone was able to get around him and he's been able to feel all the love.

"I know he really appreciates it and we love to see it.

"We all love him and happy he was able to notch up 100 games."

Arrow led his teammates out to the sound of the Gerry and the Pacemakers rendition of You'll Never Walk Alone, with 14th Immortal and dual-club legend Ron Coote ringing the Rabbitohs' bell.

The former Queensland State of Origin forward was given a guard of honour by more than 100 Souths old boys, including members of the 2021 grand final squad Arrow was a member of and his family, who all sobbed along with him and plenty of others in the stands.

"It was emotional," Roosters captain Connor Watson said in his post-match press conference.

"It was very touching. Things like that are bigger than rugby league."

Jai Arrow presented a stong face to the Rabbitohs crowd. (Getty Images: Darrian Traynor)

In the subsequent match, the Rabbitohs ran in 10 tries to pummel the Roosters 50-20, who had rested 10 of their star players with a top four spot secure.

But in completing the win, Souths have themselves earned a home finals spot, and will face Newcastle at either the Olympic Stadium or Sydney Football Stadium next week.

Campbell Graham scored twice for the Rabbitohs, who had nine different try scorers on the night, including Alex Johnston, who crossed for the 30th time this season.

Latrell Mitchell was one of them, scoring on his return to the starting line up while mixing his sublime skill with fearsome physicality, most notably when he flattened Toby Rodwell in the closing stages, standing over the stricken half like Mohammed Ali over Sonny Liston in their 1965 rematch.

If Mitchell's performance was heartening — a poor 5/10 kicking rate aside — Roosters firebrand Spencer Leniu will have raised concerns from coach Trent Robinson in the first half.

Leniu squared up to Keaon Koloamatangi after the Rabbitohs prop smashed him in a tackle twice in the same set, the second time tossing the ball away and giving away a penalty.

Titans fume over questionable calls

Earlier, the Dolphins hung on to beat the Titans 24-20 on the Gold Coast.

It was the Dolphins' seventh-consecutive win, but almost didn't happen as the Titans fought back late on and were unfortunate not to come away with the win.

The Titans were left fuming when, while leading 14-0, they had Keano Kini sin-binned in the 23rd minute for a very soft push on Dolphins winger Tevita Naufahu.

Josh Hannay was fuming after that call, and a trio of others in the closing minutes, went against his side.

"I thought it was incredibly harsh and not long after that they get a try from a knock-on," Hannay said.

"You talk about momentum swings — they don't get much bigger than that. Moe [Moeaki Fotuaika] got smacked in the face at the end and ends up in the bin for retaliating.

"[Jamayne Isaako] throws a leg out to trip [AJ Brimson] in the act of a potential try-scoring play and it is just a penalty.

"It was probably more sin-binnable than Keano's play.

"You stack all those things up and you lose by four points, you have got to be proud of your team's effort."

With AAP

Look back on how all the action unfolded in our live blog.

World.title: Woman charged with murder after body found in creek on NSW north coast
World.content:
A woman has been charged with murder after the body of a man was found in a creek on a property on the NSW north coast.

Police were called just after midday yesterday to a house on Teven Road, Teven, west of Ballina, after reports of a concern for welfare.

Officers found the body of an 81-year-old man in a creek on the property.

Police say they found the body of a man in the nearby creek. (ABC News: Lachie McLeod)

A crime scene was established, and an on-site investigation into the circumstances of the man's death is underway.

NSW Police alleged the man and woman were known to one another.

A 51-year-old woman was arrested at the scene and taken to the Lismore Police station.

A 51-year-old woman was arrested and later charged. (ABC News: Lachie McLeod)

She was later taken to Lismore Base Hospital for assessment and then released into police custody this morning, where she was returned to the station and charged with murder.

The woman was refused bail to appear before bail division court tomorrow

World.title: Clear and present Danger as Cats sweep aside Carlton
World.content:
Geelong has ended Carlton's fairytale season with a solid win, after withstanding an early challenge to run away with their elimination final.

In the first finals meeting of the two teams since the 1995 grand final, Carlton got the early jump but could not keep control, as Geelong secured the win by 33 points on a rainy night at the MCG.

Geelong skipper Patrick Dangerfield led the way with five goals in his 378th AFL game.

The loss ended Carlton's season after a monumental run of 12 wins and a draw out of 16 games to get to the elimination final under new permanent coach Josh Fraser.

Geelong will travel to Perth to face Fremantle next week in a cut-throat semifinal.

Look back at how the action unfolded in the live blog below.

World.title: Ex-MP denies he acted dishonestly in deception case
World.content:
Lawyers for former South Australian MP Fraser Ellis said he admitted he made mistakes but did not "knowingly" act dishonestly, after being convicted of seven counts of deception.

The 34-year-old former member for Narungga on the Yorke Peninsula appeared in the Adelaide Magistrates Court today ahead of sentencing for the offending, which occurred between November 2018 and May 2020.

The charges relate to the misuse of the Country Members Allowance, a fund used by regional MPs who are required to travel for parliamentary duties.

Ellis was found guilty of four counts of deception in 2024 following a trial but was acquitted of a further 19 counts.

The Director of Public Prosecutions appealed against those acquittals and three were replaced with convictions by the Court of Appeal in July this year.

Scott Henchliffe KC, for Ellis, told the court today the former MP was accused of dishonestly claiming 78 nights costing $18,095, but he was only convicted of 20 nights worth $4,676.

"He accepted that he made mistakes and he was too casual in his approach," Mr Henchliffe said.

"He maintains he did not knowingly act dishonestly."

Fraser Ellis through his lawyers says his reputation has been tarnished. (ABC News)

Mr Henchcliff rejected the idea the fraudulent claims were part of an organised plan orchestrated by Ellis and occurred in a "haphazard nature".

He argued no conviction should be recorded and a good behaviour bond should be considered.

"He feels strongly he has had his reputation tarnished by the outcome, he feels quite depressed about that," he said.

Prosecutors seek deterrence

Prosecutor James Slocombe told the court today the offending was "too serious" to proceed without recording a conviction and a short suspended prison sentence should be imposed.

"The totality of the conduct is simply more than taking from the public purse," Mr Slocombe said.

"Your Honour needs to consider the need for public deterrence in terms of an appropriate sentence."

Mr Slocombe noted Ellis had paid $24,130 as a form of restitution to the House of Assembly before charges were pursued.

Ellis was first elected as the member for Narungga in 2018 at the age of 25 but was unseated at the 2026 state election by One Nation's Chantelle Thomas.

As he left court today, Ellis told reporters he would "wait for the decision and see what happens".

He will return to court for sentencing on September 17.

World.title: ‘People might be sick of us, and they can be’: The Cats aren’t going anywhere. They might just be getting started
World.content:
Analysis SportAFLAFL 2026 ‘People might be sick of us, and they can be’: The Cats aren’t going anywhere. They might just be getting started Michael Gleeson September 5, 2026 — 1:10am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Loading

As predictable as history demands it, Geelong won a final a night after Hawthorn. Of course. Is it not always such? The Cats halted the ride of Josh Fraser’s Blues and ended what had been, according to Andrew Dillon in his pre-game speech at the AFL function, the greatest resurrection story since the Bible. Had they won, Carlton fans might argue their story is better. Yet again, Patrick Dangerfield stood strong when it counts. AFL Photos And so, with the loss, the story of the season (the football story, not the news story for the Swans presently seem to have that covered) comes to an end. The ride stopped. The wave broken. Coming from 10th, they had to find their level at some point, and leading Geelong by 21 points midway through the second term to then be overwhelmed and outplayed in the second half to lose by 33 points is their level.



Fraser cautioned at the idea that next year just picks up where this one left off, that the ride will inevitably continue and roll on into pre-season like it is “Carlton 2026: The sequel”. With the coaches’ eye for next week, Fraser preferred not to focus on how far the Blues had come in a short time this season, but how much further they still have to go. If they have brought back Carlton swagger to fill the MCG to 96,680 and the second-biggest elimination final crowd ever, there was also a crackling Carlton restlessness about where they can get to. View post on X “Tonight was disappointing, and we certainly don’t want to be a club that lives in mediocrity ... we don’t want to be a club that’s satisfied with finishing eighth,” Fraser said. “We’ve made some big improvements, there’s no doubt about that, but there are still parts of our game that we need to get to work on, and there’s some individuals that need to continue to grow. In fact, all of our players need to continue to grow.



“You know, I think there’s an expectation on the way the break looks and the way they return … I just don’t think we can turn up [in the] pre-season and think that this keeps rolling on. Related Article AFL 2026 Vintage Dangerfield breaks Blue hearts in front of more than 96,000 at the MCG “I feel like I’ve got a really good handle on where we’re at, and understand that a lot of work is in front of us.” Geelong played the role of spoiler when the sizeable Carlton portion of the crowd hoped they would carry on from the first quarter and a half in their role of straight man, as an enabler for the Blues rollicking ride. But what is momentum, Chris Scott asked rhetorically afterwards. He wished to remind us that Carlton did not have the mortgage on momentum for his side had just won six games in a row before this game. Was that not momentum? Are you not entertained?



In football, you reap what you sow and Fremantle have sown doubt, which is something of a foreign concept to the Cats. Fraser has not sown self-confidence at Carlton, for it is a club that has never lacked that trait, but he has teased it back to the surface. For all of Carlton’s brilliance over the past 15 weeks, there is something brilliant about Geelong’s past 25 years that made the gradual grind over Carlton after giving up a near four-goal lead inevitable. They overpowered the Blues with the assuredness of a side that does not understand that some clubs don’t play football in September. The Cats play finals like the best Carlton teams used to. Related Article Opinion

AFL 2026 Cats v Blues player ratings: From Geelong’s ‘Superman’, to those who had ‘horror’ nights for Carlton Danny Russell and Sam McClure Geelong now face the chastened Fremantle in Perth next week in a semi-final with Max Holmes nursing the soreness of a bloke who has rushed to be fit from an ankle injury in round 19 and had to get himself through the game. Tanner Bruhn looked proppy for much of the night, and Jeremy Cameron was still short of touch after missing five games late in the season. Scott started Cameron, who won his second Coleman Medal just last year, at half-back. We can’t say we weren’t told – Chris Scott had flagged at the end of the season that he might do it. Cameron then migrated to the wing and eventually returned forward.



Scott liked what he saw of him as a defender, but liked more what he saw of him growing into the game the longer it went on. Patrick Dangerfield kicked five goals, three of which came in the last quarter as the Cats jollied away. Last September he had a great preliminary final and then struggled to back it up the next week. This year, even with a flight to Perth for a semi-final and every week being a knockout final, Scott said Dangerfield felt “like he is coming good at the right time”. Shaun Mannagh celebrates a goal. AFL Photos The difference in Friday night’s game shifted not off the boot of the usual Geelong suspects, but the underrated Shaun Mannagh, who was excellent all night but especially so in the third quarter when his run and craft opened the game up as the Cats kicked six goals to two. The forward spent a lot more time playing midfield and continues to look like a better player the more that is asked of him. With each new step in his career, he appears get better.



“I am still a forward at heart – still a forward,” he said. “James Kelly says some funny things. He goes, ‘Everyone wants to be in a CB (centre bounce) until they’re in there, and then all hell breaks loose and everything’s on you’. So sometimes it feels like that, but a lot of us boys love that pressure and we step into it as best we can. But, nah, I’m a forward at heart.” Loading Mannagh embraced the crowd and the moment, and understood the Carlton surge. He also understood the difference in attitude to the excitement of the Blues, and his side winning a final again. “It’s another elimination game. We have an elimination [game] all the way through. We respect Fremantle like we respect Carlton, and it’s going to take our best footy again [next week], so hopefully we can do it again. Another four points (um, no).



“People might be sick of us, and they can be – we love winning, and we’ll keep doing that. We’re not going to hide from it. If you’re not trying to win, then what are you trying to do? It’s no point being in this competition. So, we’ve got a huge game next week and, hopefully, we’ve got three more games [this season].” Keep up to date with the best AFL coverage in the country.

World.title: Housing affordability craters to record low despite fall in prices
World.content:
PoliticsFederalProperty prices Housing affordability craters to record low despite fall in prices Shane Wright September 5, 2026 — 12:01am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Housing affordability has slumped to its lowest level on record, two separate measures have revealed, with falling house prices not enough to offset the financial hit delivered by the Reserve Bank’s three interest rate rises. Both realestate.com.au and the Housing Industry Association’s affordability indicators slipped in the June quarter, with some of the biggest hits to people hoping to buy in smaller capitals, while Sydney remains the nation’s least affordable city and Melbourne’s market goes sideways. Despite a drop in house prices, affordability has dropped to record lows as higher interest rates bite. Dion Georgopoulos The indicators cover the period in which the RBA lifted the cash rate from 3.6 per cent to 4.35 per cent. Financial markets put the chance of another quarter-percentage-point increase at the bank’s late September meeting at four in five. According to realestate.com.au, a median-income household earning $125,000 a year could afford just 12 per cent of all homes sold in the 2025-26 financial year. There had been a slight improvement the previous year as official interest rates fell.



Victoria is the most affordable state, where 16 per cent of homes were within financial reach, although this was down from the 19 per cent level in 2024-25. South Australia, which has gone through a surge in property prices over the past two years, is now the least affordable state, overtaking NSW, which has held that position since 2011. A median-income household in SA could afford just 7 per cent of homes sold across the state. It now takes just over six years for an average household to save a 20 per cent deposit on a median-priced home. At the turn of the century, it took three years. Senior economist with realestate.com.au, Angus Moore, said the February, March and May rate increases delivered by the Reserve Bank had added to the pressure facing people wanting to buy a home.



“Looking ahead, affordability may improve marginally if home prices continue to soften, but this is unlikely to be a turning point for many buyers,” he said. Related Article Property prices It will take a generation to fix the housing crisis, says top economist “Without a meaningful increase in housing supply, affordability will remain a significant challenge, particularly for lower-income households.” Figures released this week by property analytics firm Cotality showed house values have fallen for five consecutive months. The Commonwealth Bank is expecting price falls of up to 13 per cent in Sydney by April. The HIA’s dwelling-price-to-earnings measure has fallen in Sydney, Canberra and Melbourne since March, each city having experienced drops in prices since the RBA started lifting rates.



But affordability deteriorated in all other capital cities, with Brisbane and Perth almost as difficult to buy into as Sydney. Both cities have experienced price rises of more than 20 per cent over the past two years, though they are now starting to fall. HIA senior economist Tom Devitt said the recent lift in interest rates meant mortgage costs were climbing faster than incomes, reducing the affordability of the entire housing market. He said buyers, particularly investors, had pulled back from the market, which had led to the recent drop in prices that would probably continue through the rest of 2026. “This will not be the makings of a sustainable improvement in affordability because it does not address the fundamental demand-supply mismatch that persists in Australian housing,” he said.



“When established home prices fall but the cost of land, labour, materials, infrastructure, finance and regulation does not, fewer new housing projects are financially viable.” The drop in housing affordability may be feeding into the jobs market. Figures released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics on Friday showed a record 1.05 million people now have a second job, an 11 per cent jump over the past 12 months. More than one in 14 people holds down at least two jobs, the highest rate since the bureau started tracking the data in 1994.



The federal government has been accused by the Coalition of actively trying to push down house prices and “destroy” the wealth of Australian families. Related Article Property prices $40,000 wiped off the value of the average house over winter But Housing Minister Clare O’Neil said the government’s budget changes to property taxation, such as negative gearing, on top of its efforts to build more public and social housing, were recognition that homes were out of the reach of ordinary people. O’Neil, who on Friday opened a 285-home development in Melbourne’s south-east made up of social, affordable and market rent properties partly financed by the federal government, noted the drop in affordability was not due to the government’s budget measures. “The challenge we face is that Australian house prices have increased by around 400 per cent since 2000. If that happens again over the next generation, Australia will become a fundamentally less equal country where home ownership is beyond the reach of too many young people,” she said.



“The Coalition are the only ones remaining defending a broken status quo.” Cut through the noise of federal politics with news, views and expert analysis. Subscribers can sign up to our weekly Inside Politics newsletter.

Geelong superstar Patrick Dangerfield says he is ready to back up from tonight’s match-winning efforts against Carlton to go again in Perth next week.

Dangerfield has played 19 games in 2026 but also taken strategic rests throughout the campaign, and he said that was essential to making it to this point in the season.

Cats star Patrick Dangerfield thanks fans after the win over Carlton. Getty Images

When asked if he could back up next week in Perth, he paused to think.

“It’s a good question. Picking your moments is a big one, you can’t be in for every one,” Dangerfield told Kayo Sports.

World.title: Cats v Blues player ratings: From Geelong’s ‘Superman’, to those who had ‘horror’ nights for Carlton
World.content:
SportAFLAFL 2026 Opinion Cats v Blues player ratings: From Geelong’s ‘Superman’, to those who had ‘horror’ nights for Carlton

Loading

The fairytale had to end at some stage for the Blues, and it happened at the MCG in front of more than 96,000 fans as the finals-hardened Cats flexed their muscles right when they needed to most. Danny Russell (Geelong) and Sam McClure (Carlton) rate every Carlton player’s performance from the blockbuster elimination final. Bailey Smith celebrates on the siren after the Cats knocked the Blues out of the finals race. Getty Images Geelong



(2) Jay Polkinghorne: The latest to suffer the curse of the big forward during this finals series, he found it hard to break free and was monstered by Jacob Weitering in several marking contests but did manage a goal. 4/10 (3) Bailey Smith: Struggled to shake off a Cooper Lord tag early and would have been annoyed that his opponent kicked two goals. But he is impossible to keep down and got busy in the third. 7/10 (4) Tanner Bruhn: One of Geelong’s best early, and looks to have found his niche across half-back. He was able to become a spectator as the game wore on and the Cats shifted the match into their forward 50. 6/10 Jeremy Cameron (left) was nowhere near his best, but still walked off the ground a winner of yet another final alongside Shannon Neale and Oisin Mullin. AFL Photos (5) Jeremy Cameron: Harder to spot than Where’s Wally in the first half. He didn’t get near the footy. He started at half-back before moving to the wing, but struggled to have any meaningful impact. He’s clearly not right. 3/10



(7) Shaun Mannagh: He has yanked himself out of the “opportunist/goal sneak” pigeonhole to become a damaging midfielder. Close to the Cats’ best as he rotated through the square and found stacks of the ball. 8/10 (9) Max Holmes: Is it poor taste to say the operation was a success but the patient died? He ran the game out and, after a long lay-off, will be better for the run, but he could not find the footy and had little impact. 3/10 (11) Michael Edwards: His biggest moment was being crunched by Blake Acres in a third-quarter marking contest. It was a relief to see him get up. Other than that, he was probably shaded by Marc Pittonet in the ruck. 5/10 (14) Connor O’Sullivan: He probably wished they had another week off when the Blues came out firing in the first quarter, but was able to put the bus in cruise control thereafter. None of the big Blues got off the chain. 6/10 View post on X



(17) Lawson Humphries: Created one of the pivotal moments of the match when he spoiled a Carlton kick-in at full speed at the start of the third term. It set up a Mannagh goal, and sparked the Geelong avalanche. 5/10 Related Article AFL 2026 Dockers v Hawks player ratings: From a skipper’s career night, to the gun forwards who disappeared (21) Oliver Wiltshire: He kicked three behinds. Had they been goals, he was right up there with the game’s best players. While others shaded him on the stats sheet – he had 22 disposals – he was vital to the Cats’ turnaround. 6/10 (28) Oliver Dempsey: Even though he was short of his brilliant best, was still the game’s best winger. He took two marks deep in the forward pocket in the first and third terms, but could not convert either. 6/10 (30) Tom Atkins: He looked bamboozled, or even slow, when Sam Walsh and Jagga Smith were creating havoc in the opening term. But the never-say-die fan favourite combined with Mannagh to help swing the game back on Geelong’s terms. 6/10



(32) Gryan Miers: More reliable than a box of matches, he was one of the chief fire starters for Geelong in the second term, streaming through half-forward. Not bad for a guy on a wonky knee. He kicked two. 7/10 (33) Shannon Neale: It’s funny how the game works. He was odds-on favourite to be worst on ground in the first half, a poor showing that included a butchered shot on goal. But he lifted to kick two after the long break. 5/10 (34) Oisin Mullin: He will be popping up in Jagga Smith’s nightmares for the next six months. He was shaded by Sam Walsh in the first term before switching to the dangerous Smith and rendering him helpless. 7/10 View post on X (35) Patrick Dangerfield: Clearly the game’s best forward and best player overall. He had a touch of the Clark Kents early, fumbling some marking contests, but found the Superman cape and became unstoppable. And if that wasn’t enough, he booted five. 9/10



(36) Ollie Henry: Started on the pine and had his typical flashy moments. He needs to sit down and watch Dangerfield’s game to understand the difference between promising and delivering. 5/10 (38) Jack Henry: Another of the Cats’ unsung heroes, he provides reliable cover deep in defence that allows Tom Stewart to strut his stuff. He often picked up Harry McKay as he pushed up the ground. 6/10 (39) Zach Guthrie: With another solid night in defence, he had 16 disposals and took four marks. Not a bad output. He was instrumental in keeping the small Carlton forwards quiet. 6/10 Finals experience matters: Tom Stewart and Patrick Dangerfield were superb on the big stage yet again. AFL Photos (42) Mark O’Connor: Started on the bench before being swung into the midfield to shadow Carlton skipper Patrick Cripps. If you measure his performance on Cripps’ output (24 disposals) he’s had a good night. 6/10



(44) Tom Stewart: You can see why the Cats were lost without him in last year’s grand final. He was huge in the first half as he almost single-handedly stemmed the Carlton surge. He was big all night. 8/10 (45) Brad Close: He continues to be a poster boy for the long-sleeve brigade. He started to get busy in the second term when the Cats needed a spark, and booted a goal with his third kick of the evening. He finished with 17 disposals. 7/10 (46) Mark Blicavs: He started forward and provided cover in the ruck. He was serviceable without being responsible for any big moments. Had 19 hitouts and six tackles. 5/10 Carlton



(2) Lachlan Cowan: Held his own when the defence was under considerable pressure in the second half. 6/10 (4) Oliver Hollands: He kicked an important goal but was a bit fumbly under finals pressure. 5/10 (5) Adam Cerra: Wasn’t able to display the kind of kicking proficiency that he’s shown previously under Josh Fraser. 5/10 (7) Jagga Smith: He was unbelievable early but well-tagged in the end and his impact was reduced. 5/10 Jagga Smith was brilliant early until copping the dreaded Oisin Mullin tag. Getty Images



(9) Patrick Cripps: The skipper tried hard all night and kicked an incredible goal. 6/10 (10) Harry McKay: He presented really strongly and was probably unlucky not to get rewarded with one or two more frees. 6/10 (11) Mitch McGovern: He was terrible – he had the sort of night he’d rather forget. 2/10 (12) Ben Ainsworth: He looked likely all night but couldn’t finish like he’s been able to do all year previously. 5/10 (13) Blake Acres: He missed a sitter early but competed really hard all night. 6/10



(14) Oliver Florent: He has been a real leader in the back 50 in the second half of the year and worked hard all night again against the Blues. 7/10 (15) Billy Wilson: He has quickly become one of their most important players, finishing with 26 disposals. 7/10 (17) Brodie Kemp: He’s had a great year and still hit the scoreboard, but he does go missing from time to time. 5/10 Sam Walsh was once again the Blues’ best player in a final. AFL Photos (18) Sam Walsh: The Blues’ best player, he just continued to break lines and run both ways. 8/10



(23) Jacob Weitering: He stood up under immense pressure, especially when Harry Dean went off for his concussion test. 8/10 (27) Marc Pittonet: He dominated the ruck for large portions of the game but couldn’t use his aerial presence to great effect. 7/10 (29) George Hewett: He dug in for the majority of the night and was typically tough. 7/10 (33) Lewis Young: He had a horror night, including making inadvertent contact with Dean’s head, which forced him off for a HIA. 1/10 Harry Dean was left bloodied after copping some friendly fire. AFL Photos



(35) Harry Dean: He copped a loose boot from Young that effectively ruined his night. He still tried hard every minute he was out there. 6/10 (36) Cooper Lord: Two goals on the wing in a blockbuster MCG final is a great night. 7/10 (39) Talor Byrne: He just couldn’t find a way to have a genuine impact. 3/10 (44) Francis Evans: He was the best player on the ground early and finished with two goals. 7/10 (46) Matthew Cottrell: He plays an important role as a conduit and did some important things again in this one. 6/10

World.title: Latrell produces hit of the year as Rabbitohs crush Roosters in Arrow’s finale
World.content:
For one brutal, bone-crunching moment, all of rugby league held their breath. Except for poor old Toby Rodwell. He was trying to find it.

Latrell Mitchell, undisputed king of the NRL jungle, hit the rookie Roosters halfback with the most exquisite, most monstrous assault you could ever dish out without having to front court afterwards.

Loading

And as poor old Rodwell, 84 kilos, two games into his career, lay prone wondering what had hit him, all of rugby league wondered if Mitchell had hit him high.

Had the game’s most magnetic, single most-watchable player, just hit the kid in the head and rubbed himself out of the finals?

Nope, the replays showed. Mitchell had hit him square in the chest. Thank the big man above. Especially because Rodwell was showing signs of life. He was soon on his feet too, slowly making his way to the sideline, where Spencer Leniu had the crowd in raptures as well.

Leniu had, an hour earlier, goaded and growled at Souths fans sitting behind the Roosters bench on his way from the field. He had clashed with opposite number Keaon Koloamatangi from a kick-off, and twice again shortly afterwards, with the Rabbitohs prop winning the exchange, baiting Leniu into blowing up and a penalty being blown.

Spencer Leniu clashes with South Sydney’s Keaon Koloamatangi. NRL Photos

As the big screen cut between shots of Mitchell and Leniu, cheers rang out for the Rabbitoh, jeers for the Rooster. Leniu lapped it up, grinning with a touch of the madness that all the good front-rowers possess.

Despite the 50-20 scoreline, the Roosters had held their gloves up. In Leniu’s case, with eyes spinning like poker machines, he did so literally. Rodwell had his moments too.

And the Rabbitohs, with Jai Arrow leaving the Prime Minister emotional, along with 39,999 others at Allianz Stadium, they put their old enemy to the sword.

Before a ball was even kicked, the Dolphins’ narrow win over the Gold Coast meant the Roosters had to win or they would be locked into fourth place. Whether they head across the ditch to face New Zealand or west to take on Penrith won’t be confirmed until the final whistle of the regular season.

Loading

Barring a 41-point loss from fifth-placed Cronulla to Melbourne, the Rabbitohs will now finish sixth and host Newcastle in week one of the finals. Moments from Mitchell – even before Latrell’s scene-stealing 77th-minute shot – and David Fifita again spelled out the impact both men can have in the post-season.

When Fifita took on four defenders from dummy-half in the fifth minute, there was only going to be one winner, and the bullocking back-rower had Souths’ first try.

Tries to Bud Sullivan, Alex Johnston and Campbell Graham ensured the Rabbitohs had plenty of breathing room and a 20-4 half-time lead, before the Roosters found fortune giving the ball air.

Rex Bassingthwaighthe finished off an excellent long-range right-side shift in the 50th minute, before Butcher did the same when the Bunnies were busted up the middle a few tackles later.

But with Cody Walker pulling the strings, the veteran No.6 ensured Souths weren’t ever truly threatened. He helped himself to a try with some light stepping before Adam Elliott, Graham again, Mitchell and Brandon Smith all joined him on the scoreboard.

And Mitchell, he proved once more why he’s the biggest show in town. Just ask poor old Toby Rodwell.

World.title: The night two tribes put 120 years of feuding aside to honour Jai Arrow
World.content:
SportNRLNRL 2026 The night two tribes put 120 years of feuding aside to honour Jai Arrow Adrian Proszenko September 4, 2026 — 9:10pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Jai Arrow stepped onto South Sydney’s (sometimes) home ground. A packed house, much like the man of the moment, struggled to contain its emotions. They came for what preceded the match as much as for what occurred during it. Loading The clangs of the Legacy Bell, rung by Ron Coote, reverberated around the stadium before the opening notes of Stand By Me rang out over the PA system. And then the moment we had all come for. With both sets of players on the field, it was time for one of the most enduring sporting anthems of them all. You’ll Never Walk Alone.



Those words were also plastered on the banner Arrow walked through after emerging from the tunnel to raucous applause. Arrow, wearing jersey No.23, acknowledged the crowd. Even the Roosters players put their hands together. And thus Arrow brought up an Australian sporting century as unforgettable as any ever struck by Don Bradman. This was Arrow’s 100th and final game in the cardinal and myrtle. It was a moment imagined by Wayne Bennett, who, only a week earlier, had helped the larrikin forward put his socks on for game 99. Tonight, Bennett held the interchange card that allowed Arrow to be replaced by his great mate, Cody Walker. Everyone came together to make the milestone happen. The NRL and the players’ association granted Arrow special dispensation to “play” following his retirement after being diagnosed with Motor Neurone Disease.



There was, however, one last obstacle. The Roosters, a feuding foe for well 118 years, needed to agree. Not only did they provide their blessing, their chairman Nick Politis was one of Arrow’s most generous benefactors. “We don’t always see eye-to-eye with the Roosters, but we also know that celebrating Jai tonight will bring us all together,” said Souths chief executive Blake Solly. Jai Arrow’s wife, Berina, and daughter Ayla watch on. Wolter Peeters “On behalf of the Rabbitohs we would like to thank the Roosters for their support of Jai since his diagnosis, and we thank them for supporting this concept of Jai reaching 100 NRL games for our club.” During a half-time interview with Nine’s Danika Mason, Arrow expressed his appreciation for the support he had received.



“It means the world … for me, it’s a great moment,” Arrow said. “I’m so thankful for everyone. I love you all.” Related Article NRL 2026 Latrell produces hit of the year as Rabbitohs crush Roosters in Arrow’s finale The guard of honour comprised Rabbitohs old boys, who led fans on a march along Driver Avenue from the Sydney Cricket Ground. Among them was another past player doing it tough, Jason Death. One of the inaugural captains after the Pride of the League was reinstated into the competition, Death has been recovering from a brain bleed suffered after a fall in his Warriewood home. Yet he also wanted to pay homage to the former Maroon. Arrow’s life expectancy is unclear. Yet earlier in the day, he promised to fight on.



“No, no, don’t worry about me,” Arrow told Triple M. “I understand the disease can be very confronting. I give myself every hope to be around for 10 years, at least.” The memories he created tonight will last forever. News, results and expert analysis from the weekend of sport sent every Monday.

World.title: Brisbane’s best burger? There’s a new contender in Newstead
World.content:
Eating outFood Brisbane’s best burger? There’s a new contender in Newstead This expansive venue from one of Australia’s best craft brewers is serving classic pub fare with a fun and imaginative twist. Matt Shea September 4, 2026 Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

There are Neighbour regulars who will never visit Range Brewing, Matt McIver reckons. “And there are people who love Range for what we do – the beers, the weekly releases – who will never come to Neighbour,” says McIver, who co-owns both venues. Neighbour opened in mid-August at Gasworks Plaza. Markus Ravik If that sounds like a counterintuitive basis on which to open a new bar and eatery, McIver says to think of it as a Venn diagram: some of the punters will overlap, many won’t. Range has become good at this. When McIver and business partner Gerard Martin opened the venue in Newstead in 2018, it quickly developed a reputation for being a craft brewer’s craft brewery. Every week new beers would be released, creating a constantly rotating line-up – one that was actually worth knowing about.



Related Article Fish Lane unveils a glamorous, old-world cocktail boozer Their first expansion was a taproom in Melbourne in 2020 (it subsequently closed in 2024). But ever since, the enterprise has been more well-rounded, with strategically located venues that focus as much on food as they do beer. First there was Patio By Range in Paddington in 2023. That was followed by Rays in Camp Hill the following year. Restaurant reviews, news and the hottest openings served to your inbox. Sign up “Eight years ago, we probably didn’t foresee where this was going … But that modern culture of independent pubs having elevated food menus and nice wine lists and good beer is what we’re trying to create,” McIver says. Neighbour’s fitout feels like a reference to old-school public bars, without being too kitschy. Markus Ravik “We’re not reinventing the wheel, we’re just trying to do the classics well and with love.”



Neighbour opened late August in the Gasworks premises previously occupied by Botany, and it’s the clearest expression yet of that approach. And you can see what McIver means about the Venn diagram: the food menu could be shorthanded as the ultimate pub offering, with a bunch of classics given fun and imaginative twists. There’s a crispy-fried mozzarella in carrozza (think, a fancy cheese toastie) served with a vodka sauce; raw tuna tostadas with salsa macha, cucumber and radish; a parmigiana topped with stracciatella and fresh basil; and an Insta-worthy (and very good) wagyu cheeseburger that’s served on a bed of pepper sauce. The menu pushes pub cuisine in fun and creative directions. Markus Ravik There are also a bunch of smaller snack plates, and a woodfired pizza menu. “It’s meant to be modern Australian pub cuisine,” McIver says. “We’ve taken elements from our other venues that work well and gone from there. It’s food that’s meant to make you go, ‘I can’t stop thinking about that parmy or that steak frites’.”



For drinks, there are six taps pouring Range’s core frothies, backed by a wine list that lines up relatively esoteric Australian producers alongside drops from France and Italy. There’s also a cocktail menu that dishes up classics done “your way” alongside a bunch of approachable signatures. Neighbour’s cheeseburger is up there with the best in town. Markus Ravik All this is served in a fabulously realised fitout by Kate McLean from Soma & Sol that’s slick but welcoming, with glass-brick walls, timber panelling, tile-topped tables and high bars, and burgundy-and-cream houndstooth fabrics. It feels like a reference to old-school public bars without being too kitschy. On a Tuesday night, the place is buzzy and a manager tells me it’s been heaving on the weekends, confirming McIver and Martin’s instinct for what’s been a slightly under-loved space barely a stone’s throw from the original brewery. Neighbour’s bar is serving six tap beers alongside cocktails and small-producer wines. Markus Ravik



But it’s also another expression of a business strategy that’s become sacrosanct in craft beer circles: sell as much product as you can over your own bar. “From the get-go, it was our plan to move as much beer ourselves through our own channels as we could,” McIver says. “We’re still selling 20 kegs of beer through the new venue – that money goes straight into our bank account.” Open Mon-Thu 11am-9pm, Fri-Sat 11am-10pm, Sun 12-9pm 76 Skyring Terrace, Newstead, (07) 3110 1397 neighbourbyrange.com

World.title: ‘People might be sick of us, and they can be’: The Cats aren’t going anywhere. They might just be getting started
World.content:
Analysis SportAFLAFL 2026 ‘People might be sick of us, and they can be’: The Cats aren’t going anywhere. They might just be getting started Michael Gleeson September 5, 2026 — 1:10am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Loading

As predictable as history demands it, Geelong won a final a night after Hawthorn. Of course. Is it not always such? The Cats halted the ride of Josh Fraser’s Blues and ended what had been, according to Andrew Dillon in his pre-game speech at the AFL function, the greatest resurrection story since the Bible. Had they won, Carlton fans might argue their story is better. Yet again, Patrick Dangerfield stood strong when it counts. AFL Photos And so, with the loss, the story of the season (the football story, not the news story for the Swans presently seem to have that covered) comes to an end. The ride stopped. The wave broken. Coming from 10th, they had to find their level at some point, and leading Geelong by 21 points midway through the second term to then be overwhelmed and outplayed in the second half to lose by 33 points is their level.



Fraser cautioned at the idea that next year just picks up where this one left off, that the ride will inevitably continue and roll on into pre-season like it is “Carlton 2026: The sequel”. With the coaches’ eye for next week, Fraser preferred not to focus on how far the Blues had come in a short time this season, but how much further they still have to go. If they have brought back Carlton swagger to fill the MCG to 96,680 and the second-biggest elimination final crowd ever, there was also a crackling Carlton restlessness about where they can get to. View post on X “Tonight was disappointing, and we certainly don’t want to be a club that lives in mediocrity ... we don’t want to be a club that’s satisfied with finishing eighth,” Fraser said. “We’ve made some big improvements, there’s no doubt about that, but there are still parts of our game that we need to get to work on, and there’s some individuals that need to continue to grow. In fact, all of our players need to continue to grow.



“You know, I think there’s an expectation on the way the break looks and the way they return … I just don’t think we can turn up [in the] pre-season and think that this keeps rolling on. Related Article AFL 2026 Vintage Dangerfield breaks Blue hearts in front of more than 96,000 at the MCG “I feel like I’ve got a really good handle on where we’re at, and understand that a lot of work is in front of us.” Geelong played the role of spoiler when the sizeable Carlton portion of the crowd hoped they would carry on from the first quarter and a half in their role of straight man, as an enabler for the Blues rollicking ride. But what is momentum, Chris Scott asked rhetorically afterwards. He wished to remind us that Carlton did not have the mortgage on momentum for his side had just won six games in a row before this game. Was that not momentum? Are you not entertained?



In football, you reap what you sow and Fremantle have sown doubt, which is something of a foreign concept to the Cats. Fraser has not sown self-confidence at Carlton, for it is a club that has never lacked that trait, but he has teased it back to the surface. For all of Carlton’s brilliance over the past 15 weeks, there is something brilliant about Geelong’s past 25 years that made the gradual grind over Carlton after giving up a near four-goal lead inevitable. They overpowered the Blues with the assuredness of a side that does not understand that some clubs don’t play football in September. The Cats play finals like the best Carlton teams used to. Related Article Opinion

AFL 2026 Cats v Blues player ratings: From Geelong’s ‘Superman’, to those who had ‘horror’ nights for Carlton Danny Russell and Sam McClure Geelong now face the chastened Fremantle in Perth next week in a semi-final with Max Holmes nursing the soreness of a bloke who has rushed to be fit from an ankle injury in round 19 and had to get himself through the game. Tanner Bruhn looked proppy for much of the night, and Jeremy Cameron was still short of touch after missing five games late in the season. Scott started Cameron, who won his second Coleman Medal just last year, at half-back. We can’t say we weren’t told – Chris Scott had flagged at the end of the season that he might do it. Cameron then migrated to the wing and eventually returned forward.



Scott liked what he saw of him as a defender, but liked more what he saw of him growing into the game the longer it went on. Patrick Dangerfield kicked five goals, three of which came in the last quarter as the Cats jollied away. Last September he had a great preliminary final and then struggled to back it up the next week. This year, even with a flight to Perth for a semi-final and every week being a knockout final, Scott said Dangerfield felt “like he is coming good at the right time”. Shaun Mannagh celebrates a goal. AFL Photos The difference in Friday night’s game shifted not off the boot of the usual Geelong suspects, but the underrated Shaun Mannagh, who was excellent all night but especially so in the third quarter when his run and craft opened the game up as the Cats kicked six goals to two. The forward spent a lot more time playing midfield and continues to look like a better player the more that is asked of him. With each new step in his career, he appears get better.



“I am still a forward at heart – still a forward,” he said. “James Kelly says some funny things. He goes, ‘Everyone wants to be in a CB (centre bounce) until they’re in there, and then all hell breaks loose and everything’s on you’. So sometimes it feels like that, but a lot of us boys love that pressure and we step into it as best we can. But, nah, I’m a forward at heart.” Loading Mannagh embraced the crowd and the moment, and understood the Carlton surge. He also understood the difference in attitude to the excitement of the Blues, and his side winning a final again. “It’s another elimination game. We have an elimination [game] all the way through. We respect Fremantle like we respect Carlton, and it’s going to take our best footy again [next week], so hopefully we can do it again. Another four points (um, no).



“People might be sick of us, and they can be – we love winning, and we’ll keep doing that. We’re not going to hide from it. If you’re not trying to win, then what are you trying to do? It’s no point being in this competition. So, we’ve got a huge game next week and, hopefully, we’ve got three more games [this season].” Keep up to date with the best AFL coverage in the country.

World.title: Housing affordability craters to record low despite fall in prices
World.content:
PoliticsFederalProperty prices Housing affordability craters to record low despite fall in prices Shane Wright September 5, 2026 — 12:01am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Housing affordability has slumped to its lowest level on record, two separate measures have revealed, with falling house prices not enough to offset the financial hit delivered by the Reserve Bank’s three interest rate rises. Both realestate.com.au and the Housing Industry Association’s affordability indicators slipped in the June quarter, with some of the biggest hits to people hoping to buy in smaller capitals, while Sydney remains the nation’s least affordable city and Melbourne’s market goes sideways. Despite a drop in house prices, affordability has dropped to record lows as higher interest rates bite. Dion Georgopoulos The indicators cover the period in which the RBA lifted the cash rate from 3.6 per cent to 4.35 per cent. Financial markets put the chance of another quarter-percentage-point increase at the bank’s late September meeting at four in five. According to realestate.com.au, a median-income household earning $125,000 a year could afford just 12 per cent of all homes sold in the 2025-26 financial year. There had been a slight improvement the previous year as official interest rates fell.



Victoria is the most affordable state, where 16 per cent of homes were within financial reach, although this was down from the 19 per cent level in 2024-25. South Australia, which has gone through a surge in property prices over the past two years, is now the least affordable state, overtaking NSW, which has held that position since 2011. A median-income household in SA could afford just 7 per cent of homes sold across the state. It now takes just over six years for an average household to save a 20 per cent deposit on a median-priced home. At the turn of the century, it took three years. Senior economist with realestate.com.au, Angus Moore, said the February, March and May rate increases delivered by the Reserve Bank had added to the pressure facing people wanting to buy a home.



“Looking ahead, affordability may improve marginally if home prices continue to soften, but this is unlikely to be a turning point for many buyers,” he said. Related Article Property prices It will take a generation to fix the housing crisis, says top economist “Without a meaningful increase in housing supply, affordability will remain a significant challenge, particularly for lower-income households.” Figures released this week by property analytics firm Cotality showed house values have fallen for five consecutive months. The Commonwealth Bank is expecting price falls of up to 13 per cent in Sydney by April. The HIA’s dwelling-price-to-earnings measure has fallen in Sydney, Canberra and Melbourne since March, each city having experienced drops in prices since the RBA started lifting rates.



But affordability deteriorated in all other capital cities, with Brisbane and Perth almost as difficult to buy into as Sydney. Both cities have experienced price rises of more than 20 per cent over the past two years, though they are now starting to fall. HIA senior economist Tom Devitt said the recent lift in interest rates meant mortgage costs were climbing faster than incomes, reducing the affordability of the entire housing market. He said buyers, particularly investors, had pulled back from the market, which had led to the recent drop in prices that would probably continue through the rest of 2026. “This will not be the makings of a sustainable improvement in affordability because it does not address the fundamental demand-supply mismatch that persists in Australian housing,” he said.



“When established home prices fall but the cost of land, labour, materials, infrastructure, finance and regulation does not, fewer new housing projects are financially viable.” The drop in housing affordability may be feeding into the jobs market. Figures released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics on Friday showed a record 1.05 million people now have a second job, an 11 per cent jump over the past 12 months. More than one in 14 people holds down at least two jobs, the highest rate since the bureau started tracking the data in 1994.



The federal government has been accused by the Coalition of actively trying to push down house prices and “destroy” the wealth of Australian families. Related Article Property prices $40,000 wiped off the value of the average house over winter But Housing Minister Clare O’Neil said the government’s budget changes to property taxation, such as negative gearing, on top of its efforts to build more public and social housing, were recognition that homes were out of the reach of ordinary people. O’Neil, who on Friday opened a 285-home development in Melbourne’s south-east made up of social, affordable and market rent properties partly financed by the federal government, noted the drop in affordability was not due to the government’s budget measures. “The challenge we face is that Australian house prices have increased by around 400 per cent since 2000. If that happens again over the next generation, Australia will become a fundamentally less equal country where home ownership is beyond the reach of too many young people,” she said.



“The Coalition are the only ones remaining defending a broken status quo.” Cut through the noise of federal politics with news, views and expert analysis. Subscribers can sign up to our weekly Inside Politics newsletter.

Cats star Patrick Dangerfield thanks fans after the win over Carlton. Getty Images
